# Race geometry research candidate, based on v0.33

This is an isolated test extension, version 0.33.1. It adds an optional recorder, not a new driving or braking feature. It has not been tested in a live race. Existing v0.33 controls and settings are unchanged. Disable other copies of Driving Tools before loading this candidate, and keep the working v0.33 folder for rollback.

## What it records

The recorder reads the owned driver's native race-planning window at the point where the game finishes its corner pass. It does not use free-roam GPS, the drawn map, screenshots, unrestricted asset downloads or opponent routes.

- Off by default, session-only, separate from all driving settings.
- Exact game build 93af6ccb only. Unknown builds do not activate it.
- Offline single-player ordinary race AI only. Online/LAN, drag, drift, special-mode flags, free roam and unsupported ownership are excluded, regardless of the existing online toggle.
- At most 256 windows, no faster than 10 requests/second, at most 40 nodes and 5 corner records per window. The recorder does not enable AI itself.
- No new native calls, steering, throttle, brake, target-speed, tuning, race-state or opponent writes. New writes are confined to its local 2 KiB request/response mailbox.
- Stops on observed identity/state changes, hidden/inactive tab, Stop, manual-control handback, game exit or timeout. An unsettled request or occupied mailbox requires a reload instead of automatic retries.
- Export is a local JSON download. Nothing is uploaded or stored in a tool profile.

## First bounded offline check

1. Keep a backup of progress. Disable other Driving Tools copies, load this candidate's `extension` folder as an unpacked extension, and reload the game once. No reload or installation has been performed for you.
2. Start an offline ordinary road race. Use the existing AI setting only if you want it to drive. Keep your existing working controls unchanged; capture does not require stronger pace, power, NOS or braking settings.
3. Open Session & diagnostics → Race geometry research → Record native route samples. Keep the tab focused. Stop after a short run, then choose Export route samples. Export before reload/closing; re-arming starts a new recording.

If the recorder reports zero sampled corner records, unknown data, a timeout or an unsupported state, report that result rather than assuming the road is straight. Export the partial recording if available. Do not repeatedly re-arm an unsettled request. Stop testing if the game behaves unexpectedly, and restore the working v0.33 extension.

## Meaning of the 75-degree analysis

The threshold is change of forward heading: 0° straight, 90° right-angle, 180° reversal. The analyzer combines same-direction turns within an ordered native record, so several gentler changes can reach 75°. Opposite-direction bends remain separate. Curvature below 75° is retained because a shallower bend may still need slowing at high speed.

Fresh side-sample markers, finite XY/distances and strictly increasing native distances are required before a record is treated as ordered. Duplicate points, missing pages, stale native tails, non-finite values, invalid ordering and excessive spacing remain unknown. An apparently straight map or straight chord is never proof that the underlying road is straight.

This analyzes sampled horizontal chords. It does not yet assemble windows into a complete race, verify the underlying spline between samples, detect all gentle bends spanning multiple windows, or measure altitude/banking. The native center is reused as the game's center; it is not claimed newly regenerated every pass.

## Identity and coverage

Career records include a verified event hash and native heat ordinal when the native pointer/count, event tuple, track, reverse and laps agree. Region is copied from a bounded TrackInfo field, and TrackInfo's track must agree. Quick-race career event/heat is explicitly unknown. Observed clock resets and career start-counter changes stop recording, but no universal attempt counter or perfect restart detection is claimed.

Each window remains partial. Repeated records are not unique-corner counts. Export always says `wholeRaceChecked:false` and `uniqueCornersVerified:false`. Actual complete race routes captured or verified so far: zero. This is not an “all corners protected” release and does not establish safer braking, faster laps or fewer collisions.

## Offline checks completed

- 28 new synthetic/loader/UI/preservation tests.
- 15 reader/geometry tests, including 144 synthetic unequal-segment triples checked against the exact native curvature helper.
- 1,930 existing v0.33 regression tests. Release-packaging tests and signature-report writers were excluded from this copied regression harness; separate candidate packaging checks are recorded with the research artifacts.
- The complete modified module validates and compiles. Compared with the verified v0.33 patch, only the intended route-updater function differs, and all its original instructions are retained.

Synthetic tests and compilation do not replace live validation. The next useful input is a short offline JSON capture, followed by route-order, coverage and braking-horizon validation. No automatic slowing based on this recorder has been enabled.

## v0.33.0: Continuous adaptive corner targets

Adaptive road-race speed now has a separate native planning command. Every valid sampled nonzero bend receives a smooth curvature-based target, instead of requiring it to cross the older curvature threshold. Exact straights keep the requested target ceiling; existing native lower/stop results are never increased. The native distance-based braking calculation uses the same pace compensation.

The curve is deliberately conservative and experimental. It does not detect every corner on the map: the native planner may provide no corner records, skip a tail record, report zero curvature or use another route. It does not change steering, physical brakes, route lookahead, NOS or other cars. A hook hit is an observation of a past call, not proof the current corner is safe. Five fresh captures show hook hits despite reported missed turns, so the update is not presented as a proven fix for every failure.

Only adaptive road mode uses this new command. **Street X and existing free-roam/road-corner controls retain their exact prior behavior.** The new command also denies actual/forced Street X and known online Street X in its native guards. AI ownership, native handback, online permission, mode checks and watchdog remain required. This does not bypass an AI failure or acquire control automatically.

The option remains default-off/session-only and uses your current sliders without changing saved values. For the first comparison, try the existing defaults: 1.30× adaptive ceiling, 0.80 corner factor and 0.75 braking factor. Higher targets can still cause missed turns. The latest logs used 1.90×, 0.95 and 1.00 respectively; those settings were confirmed, not shown to be safe. Keep the working Street X setup unchanged.

Corner/braking hit counters now use the existing two-second telemetry sample cadence instead of replacing bounded history every quarter second. Discrete control/mode changes still log promptly. No raw route geometry, memory dump or additional personal data is collected.

Saved tool profiles, full preset tuning, online road-race/collision controls and Drag blowout protection remain combined. The combined suite passes **1,698 tests, zero failures/skips/cancellations**. No live Drift run, score improvement, browser installation or game-save persistence is claimed. For a useful comparison, use the same car, track and tune; export a short diagnostic log after a run that reproduces the problem.

## Retained v0.25.0: Saved extension settings profiles

**Saved tool profiles** saves named groups of extension settings in this browser for this game site. Save your current choices, then load them together instead of enabling each tool separately. Update replaces the selected saved configuration; Delete removes it. These profiles are separate from the game's race tuning presets and **Save Profile**. They contain no car setup, game save, dyno draft or diagnostic log.

Automatic loading after reload is **optional and off by default**. Select it explicitly for a saved configuration if you want that configuration to return next time. Network permission has a separate saved-profile opt-in: saved choices do not silently grant Online/LAN access. Read the network warning before permitting automatic network-enabled behavior. Each tool still requires the supported build, valid current car and its normal game-mode checks.

**F9 / Stop keeps saved profiles but pauses automatic loading persistently**, as well as clearing current driving/network choices. A later reload cannot silently undo Stop. Resume deliberately from the profile controls. Saving a profile does not itself enable its settings. Changes from another tab do not automatically activate a configuration in an already-open tab.

Profile loading stops the old controllers and releases synthetic input before changing selections. It does not roll back a staged game tune or save the game. If storage is unavailable or full, the UI reports that the profile was not saved. Profiles stay in this browser; clearing this site's storage removes them, and site scripts can access this storage. Up to 16 profiles and 48 characters per name are supported. Browser-managed locking prevents concurrent tabs from overwriting each other's saves; if locking is unavailable, profile editing is disabled while manual loading remains available.

Saved Drag blowout protection retains its narrow meaning: only the current eligible local engine is protected before it blows; online use also needs network permission. It does not revive an already-blown engine, alter NOS/shifting, or promise a race win. Existing controls keep their normal fresh-page defaults unless you explicitly enable a saved startup profile. Descriptions below that say a control starts off refer to those defaults.

No native AI, Street X, tuning, heat, corner/braking or collision payload was changed for settings profiles. The final suite passes 1,688 tests, with another 44 independent profile checks. A local Chromium fixture could not launch because this environment denied socket creation, so browser appearance and automatic loading in the user's game remain unverified.

## Signature scanning and build updates

The loader performs a read-only scan against three reviewed sets of 34 typed function fingerprints. It reports unique, ambiguous and missing matches in local diagnostics, plus the actual module hash. The menu retains the full compatibility explanation rather than truncating it. AI and Dyno now give the same explicit unavailable-build reason instead of suggesting the wrong tuning screen.

**Signature matches do not automatically authorize a new game version.** Matching functions alone do not establish callees, dispatch tables, host addresses, scratch ownership or live behavior. Even 34/34 matches on a different binary leave tools disabled until an exact compatibility profile has been reviewed. This is update diagnosis, not a promise that future game updates will work automatically. Scanner failure does not override the independent exact-binary gate.

## Automatic AI race-type switching

Turn on **AI driver → Automatic driver** once per page. It automatically selects:

- **Non-drag races and free roam:** the existing native player autopilot.
- **Drag:** experimental native racer AI with the verified drag physics type. It waits until GO and full driving physics are available.
- **Changing mode:** requests native AI OFF, waits for the game thread to acknowledge it, confirms ownership is released, the human driver is restored and any failed-acquisition latch is cleared, then requests the new mode. Player, car, race, track, drag/drift/URL/StreetX flags, forced native mode flags and race/free-roam changes are checked, including when object pointers are reused.

There is no separate drag-AI checkbox. The main switch explicitly enables automatic selection, including experimental drag. **You still start events yourself. This does not select races, restart them, navigate career menus, buy upgrades or choose a GPS destination.** It includes the separate experimental free-roam corner-speed and dyno-search tools described below. They are off by default.

The extension requests the game's native player autopilot, not a new steering bot. The native constructor chooses a distinct drift behavior and a shared ordinary/drag/StreetX behavior; its update code contains drag-specific branches. Circuit, sprint, URL and outrun do not have separately proven opponent-equivalent implementations here. The player racer identity stays unchanged. “Level 9” means the ordinary native skill field is set to 9; values 254/255 are preserved. We have not proved that drag's launch, shifting or lane decisions consume that field.

**Live drag driving remains unverified.** Correct driver/physics status does not prove that it shifts, steers, avoids traffic or finishes. It may crash, stop or miss checkpoints. Back up your progress and test solo first. No guaranteed routes, perfect drift, wins or completed races.

### Quick start

1. Back up your save with the game's **Download backup** button.
2. Keep your previous extension folder for rollback. Disable its extension card before loading this version.
3. Extract this ZIP. In `chrome://extensions` (Edge: `edge://extensions`), enable Developer mode and choose **Load unpacked**. Select **NFSU2-Driving-Tools-v0.29.0**, containing `manifest.json`.
4. Reload the game and check version **0.29.0**. Only one version should be enabled.
5. Start a solo event yourself. Open Driving tools with **F8**, then enable **Automatic driver** in a non-drag event. For your first drag test, leave power, grip, NOS, custom pace, collision filters and manual Drag assist off.
6. Enter other supported events normally. AI requests native handback/reconstruction automatically when the event changes. Turn AI off before using manual drag assist. Other selected settings are kept.

Chrome 111+ or a compatible current Chromium browser is required. This is not a Firefox or mobile-browser build. No build tools or Node installation are needed to install the extension.

### Take control and pause

- **F7 / Take control:** disables automatic AI until you explicitly turn it on again. Arrow/WASD keys and Space also take control outside the extension menu. This remains off across later race-type changes.
- Controller axes do not trigger takeover; use F7 or the Take control button.
- Taking control also pauses synthetic manual-drag throttle until you toggle manual Drag assist again.
- **F9 / Stop:** clears automatic AI, all four collision switches, Online/LAN permission, custom pace, NOS, power, limiter, grip and manual drag. Slider values are retained. Drift and the read-only tester keep their own switches.
- Menus, loading, unfocused/hidden tabs and unsupported states pause tools without clearing choices. They resume when a supported driving state returns, unless you took manual control.
- **Automatic AI, wall pass-through, solo car no-clip, online traffic no-clip, corner assist, both pace opt-ins, power boost, limiter removal, extra grip, dyno tuner and Online/LAN permission start OFF after every page reload.** Other settings use same-tab session storage. Closing the tab normally ends those saved choices. Storage may be unavailable or affected by browser restore behavior.
- If the page stops updating, native AI hands back within 180 game frames. A frozen game cannot process a handback. Disable the extension and reload if it freezes.

## Compact menu

The menu starts as a **170 × 29 px** collapsed toolbar and opens to a **244 px** drawer with a 390 px maximum scroll panel. **F8** opens/closes it. Sections start folded, only one main section opens at a time, and longer sections scroll. Help and detailed status are tucked away; no control was removed. **F7 / Take control** and **F9 / Stop** remain keyboard shortcuts, with buttons in the open toolbar.

## Independent controls

### AI and pace

The native AI switch uses player-only skill **9**, the highest normal native value. It restores the original value when the same racer still exists. Special sentinels are left unchanged and are not claimed as level 9. It does not alter other racers or commandeer an AI driver the extension did not acquire.

**Free-roam pace:** 0.75×–3.00× for native free roam only, default off / 1.00×. Its factor is saved, but its switch starts off after reload.

**Race / outrun pace:** a separate 0.75×–3.00× opt-in, default off / 1.00×. Its value is saved, but its switch starts off after reload. Your faster free-roam choice does not carry into races.

Both adjust the native target-speed factor, not engine power, steering or road paths. **2–3× pace is especially experimental: severe overspeed, missed turns/checkpoints and instability are possible.** No real driving at those factors has been verified. Drag, dyno and unknown categories use neutral 1.00×. The choices remain selected while ineligible and resume only in their own category. F7 leaves them dormant; F9 clears both switches. They never turn AI on by themselves.

### Free-roam corner-speed assist

A separate, experimental opt-in reduces the native planner's curvature-limited speed for upcoming free-roam corners. It does not replace steering or road paths. Its bounded factor is **0.60–0.95**, starting at **0.80**. Straight/gentle segments retain their native speed cap. This factor is a tuning hypothesis, not a measured optimum.

**Sharp-turn margin** adds 0–25% extra reduction, starting at 15%, according to how far the native corner speed falls below its maximum cap. Tighter upcoming bends receive more margin. The combined formula is `nativeCornerSpeed × baseFactor × (1 − margin/100 × (1 − nativeCornerSpeed/nativeMaximumSpeed))`. At 0%, it follows the v0.13 calculation exactly. With the strongest settings the effective factor can approach 0.45×; it never changes a straight-cap result. This adjusts the original planner’s speed cap, not its steering or proven sampling distance. Begin with normal 1× pace and power/grip changes off, comparing 0% and 15% on the same solo route.

It applies only to the current, owned AI driver's private main route in native free roam. Races, outruns, drag, drift and the Dyno Shop are excluded. Changing its enabled state, factor or sharp-turn margin rebuilds AI through a full native OFF/manual/ON handoff, because the game caches route speed caps. Free-roam/race transitions also rebuild before rearming.

**Corner status:** Armed means a request is present, not that a qualifying native reduction has been confirmed. Straight/gentle calls and guarded calls add no hit. Occupied command memory and observed drift exclusion are reported separately. The crash log now records bounded corner hits, request state, applied factor and those two observable guards. Confirmed pace is a different acknowledgment and does not prove corner assist ran. For diagnosis, use 1× pace; 0.95× corner factor reduces a qualifying corner cap by only 5%. A persistent no-hit result after bends is still unresolved without live telemetry.

It may help turn entry but cannot repair a bad route, prevent crashes, guarantee a clean corner or improve lap times. More power, grip or pace may undermine it. Live braking, route rebuilding and handling improvements remain unverified. Start conservatively and keep F7 available.

### Full per-race preset tuner

Use the **solo Performance Tuning main screen** on exact 93af6ccb. Back up your save, select a race preset in the game, then enable the tuner. It never buys upgrades, switches the game's preset, enters a race or presses Save Profile.

1. **Load selected preset** captures the current car, installed parts, working tune and selected visit tune on the game thread. The editor displays all 41 settings in their native categories and disables fields locked by installed parts/native rules.
2. Change sliders and press **Preview draft**. Native setters and rebuild/measurement functions run only in a separate memory copy. The preview shows accepted values, including native coupled changes, and comparable before/after estimates. Your live setup remains unchanged.
3. Alternatively choose a measured goal and press **Find tune**. Peak power/torque searches ECU/turbo; 0–60, 0–100 and top speed search gearing plus ECU/turbo. Search is capped at 48 trials. It keeps manual suspension, brake, tire, aero and NOS choices, but does not optimize their handling or lap-time effects. A faster estimated acceleration can reduce top speed; inspect all results.
4. **Stage selected preset** is an explicit separate action. It accepts only the last successfully evaluated candidate, on the same car, preset, installed parts and unchanged setup/visit/record. A game-thread transaction copies just the current 41-byte tune and selected 41-byte visit tune. Other presets and the saved-car record are not written by this action.
5. Start the game's own **Test Run** to refresh driving physics and check the tune. Merely exiting the tuning screen is not a verified rebuild. Use the game's **Save Profile** to persist changes. The game's save can commit all five visit presets, so the tuner warns when other visit presets differ from their stored record. “Save ready” is not a successful save confirmation.
6. **Restore previous** needs the same car, preset, parts and exact last-staged tune. It restores the original current and selected visit tunes, even when those originally differed. A known native commit of this exact selected tune is accepted; unrelated record changes are refused. Restore does not undo disk saves. Use Test Run and Save Profile again if you want the restored state refreshed and persisted.

Each car/preset has separate guarded restore state while the page stays open. A car replacement, manual edits, changed parts or an unknown record change invalidates stale results. Reload loses this temporary restore history. Native unlocked gear counts and tuning rules remain authoritative; no sixth gear is invented. Sliders display −100 to +100 around the game's neutral value, stored internally as bytes 0–200. These are normalized settings, not physical units.

The measurements are native estimates, not lap times or on-track benchmarks. Handling controls and NOS expose native settings without a proven per-race optimal objective. There are no claimed “perfect” race presets, global optimum, guaranteed wins or proven save/reload result. The previous peak-only dyno tool remains on older supported builds with its existing guarded Apply/Restore flow.

Cancel, F9, closing the panel, blur, a hidden tab, leaving the page or disabling the tuner cancels ongoing work. Driving effects pause during work, with their selections retained. **F9 does not undo a tune already staged.** Re-enable the tuner and use Restore previous while its baseline remains valid. A timed-out game-thread request has an uncertain outcome and disables further writes until reload; inspect the game rather than blindly retrying.

The private evaluator extracts only reviewed native functions from the exact game module already downloaded by the browser. It has its own memory, checked capture ranges, write allowlist and operation budget. Capture/stage/restore run through a command-gated frame prefix with no native calls and no profile-file writes. This bounds the reviewed path but is not a guarantee against browser exhaustion, unrelated game faults or live object-lifetime races.

### Power and handling

- **Unlimited NOS:** refills an already equipped kit while driving; does not install a kit or force native AI to activate NOS.
- **Power boost:** 1.0×–3.0× engine and nitrous torque. Starts at 1.5×. Repeated updates do not compound. More power can worsen wheelspin and handling.
- **Remove stock limiter:** removes the stock MPH governor while enabled. Gearing, drag and redline still limit speed. Upgraded cars may already lack that governor.
- **Extra grip:** 1.0×–2.0× all four tyre-force factors. Starts at 1.3×. It is not auto-steering, yaw damping, corner avoidance or guaranteed handling. High grip can cause abrupt behavior or rollover. It pauses in drift mode/races.
- Power and grip restore only fields still owned by the extension. They wait for three matching samples before applying to rebuilt car data. Changed external tuning is preserved rather than overwritten. Pause/off restores owned values when the original live objects remain valid.
- **Drift assist:** uses the game's real drift-event input and waits for its handling confirmation. Solo free roam only, with game menus closed. It is not perfect-drift automation. Power/grip restore before the native tuning rebuild; settings stay selected. Drift uses its own switch, including after F9.

### Wall / barrier pass-through

**Handling & collisions → Wall pass-through** is independent of AI and **solo-only**, even with Online/LAN tools allowed. Turn **Free roam with others** off, or use a solo race.

Only contacts between your car and verified near-vertical static track polygons are skipped, using the native wall threshold `abs(normal.z) < 0.1`. Ground, ceilings, ramps/slopes and movable props retain the original collision path. Cars retain it unless the independent Car no-clip option is enabled. Sloped faces and movable barrier props remain solid. This is not unrestricted flight or universal noclip. The game's native Ghost setting affects cars, not walls; the extension leaves that setting unchanged.

A selected checkbox is not proof of contact filtering. Its status first says Armed, then counts contacts actually skipped by the native hook. Test a plain vertical wall and neon barrier at low speed; verify ground/ramp and car collisions yourself. Coverage has not been live-verified.

You may leave the drivable map, miss checkpoints or get stuck inside scenery. Native recovery may reposition you after a reset. **Turn it off only when clear of a wall.** Off/F9/reload restores the original collision path. It does not change shared map objects or body collision flags.

### Solo Car no-clip

**Handling & collisions → Car no-clip** is separate from Wall pass-through and is solo-only. It matches confirmed native car collision bodies paired with the current local player's car, whether driven manually or by AI. It does not skip collisions between other cars. Walls, ground and props retain their normal path unless the wall option separately applies.

It starts off after reload and reports Armed until a supported contact is actually skipped. Turn it off only once clear of other cars. F9 stops it. No body flags or shared map objects are changed. Native constructor/category and current wrapper tests pass, but real traffic/racer collisions have not been live-verified.

### Online traffic no-clip

**Handling & collisions → Online traffic no-clip** is a separate switch, available on exact builds **93af6ccb and 78e2bb69**. It requires online free roam and matches native NPC traffic paired with your local car, driven manually or by AI. It excludes native player-slot cars even if they use a traffic model or traffic driver flag, plus ordinary AI racers, every race category, outruns and Online/LAN races. Other players and rejected contacts retain the game's original collision logic, including any native Ghost choice you made. Walls, ground, props, body flags and map objects are unchanged.

This switch starts **off after every reload**, even if previously selected. It needs its own explicit opt-in; **Allow Online/LAN tools** never enables it. That general permission is not required for this narrowly scoped online-free-roam traffic switch. Solo Car no-clip stays independent. The status distinguishes Armed from observed traffic contacts skipped. F9 stops and clears it; blur, hidden tabs, dyno work and unavailable driving state pause it. Turn it off only when clear of traffic.

No live online collisions, peer synchronization or server acceptance have been verified. It changes local contact resolution, not the traffic simulation or server rules. Follow the site's rules and use an explicitly permitted private test. A selected or Armed switch is not proof that a real contact was skipped.

### Manual drag assist

A separate, optional throttle / RPM-threshold shift / NOS helper **while you steer**. Uses default Arrow Up, Left Shift and Left Alt bindings. Set shift RPM for your car; 6500 is only a starting point, not learned perfect shifting.

Manual drag assist never runs while automatic drag AI is requested, including countdown and failed/unavailable AI. It will not silently substitute synthetic inputs. With Automatic AI off, manual drag waits for native ownership to clear and a human driver to be confirmed. Countdown permits throttle only; shifts and NOS wait for GO. It does not choose lanes or avoid obstacles. F7/manual takeover pauses it until its switch is toggled again.

### Diagnostics

#### Local crash log

Open **Driving tools → Session & diagnostics → Crash log → Export crash log**. This downloads `nfsu2-driving-tools-diagnostics.json` on your computer. Nothing is automatically sent or uploaded. **Clear log** removes this tab's retained diagnostic history; recording then continues.

The logger starts when this extension page loads. It records recent tool choices/factors, sampled game mode and driver state, page/game-worker lifecycle, classified errors, numeric WebAssembly function/offset locations and line numbers from known script files. It does not capture raw console logs, error messages, URLs, credentials, names, saves, keyboard input or network traffic. It never changes game memory or enables a tool.

The newest **180 events, limited to 64 KiB of stored JSON**, are kept in same-tab session storage. State is sampled on discrete changes (at most four times a second), moving native scalars about every two seconds, and a baseline snapshot every five seconds while driving; rapid repeated page errors are capped. Older entries are discarded and the file reports the count. Export soon after a problem. Reloading the same tab normally retains the log; closing the tab, clearing site data, browser recovery behavior or blocked/full storage can lose it. The menu reports when the log is memory-only. The site's own scripts can access this same-origin session storage, so it is not an extension-private vault.

**Capture limits:** this cannot recover crashes that happened before the logger was installed. A full browser/tab/GPU crash, freeze or forced close may prevent any final event. This is a history of observations, not a complete crash dump or proof of the crash's cause; the last snapshot may precede the failure. Free-text errors are deliberately omitted for privacy, so unfamiliar errors appear as `other`. Also export the game's own **Download log** for native game details. This logger does not fix the reported crash or establish that the game is safe.


The read-only traffic/barrier tester reads nearby car objects and the enabled barrier-line table. It is incomplete: it does not fully classify traffic/racers, shapes, props, road geometry, elevation or safe lanes. No detected obstacle does not imply a safe road.

## Online / LAN

Online/LAN remains blocked by default for existing tools. The separate **Session mode → Allow Online/LAN tools** switch is per-page and starts off on reload. It does not activate individual tools. It never overrides the solo restrictions on walls and solo Car no-clip, drag physics requirements, pause checks or one-local-player checks. Online traffic no-clip remains online-free-roam-only. Current-build Online player / race no-clip requires its own selection plus network permission for the race path; only local contacts are affected.

Online modifications may affect racers, trigger integrity checks, invalidate results or cause moderation/bans. Follow the site's rules and prefer solo play or an explicitly permitted private test. This extension does not bypass server restrictions. Turning off the session switch stops AI/synthetic keys and restores owned tuning when possible, while keeping selections for solo. NOS already refilled is not drained. F9 clears the permission.

## Validation and known limits

**Automated validation:** the final v0.28 suite passes **1,740 tests, zero failures/skips/cancellations**, including high-address runtime CPU cases. See `CHANGELOG.md`. The frozen v0.20 tuner baseline passed 1,599 tests. Coverage includes the retained v0.18 regressions, actual native isolated getter/setter/rebuild and metrics, all unlocked control offsets, exact game-thread capture/stage/restore, all five preset leases, stale-state/identity/cancellation/fuel guards, and end-to-end private preview with selected-preset-only writes. The end-to-end harness uses exact native game functions and a constructed car/catalog fixture, not a live user's game. Focused suites overlap and are not additive totals. These checks are not a full game simulation or live gameplay.

All four exact supported modules validate and compile after patching. Both modern profiles change12 bodies: **2459, 3174, 4497, 4653, 7395, 8871, 17404, 19197, 19277, 21213, 21263**, plus contact wrapper **22508** on93af6ccb or **22470** on78e2bb69. On2f0ddd3b, only **4497, 4653, 21213, 21262 and22430** change; on6f4f1e4e, only **4497, 4653, 21213, 21262 and22720** change. Every other function body and non-code section is preserved byte-for-byte. Original planner instructions and contact-wrapper tails remain preserved. The native Drift recovery expression replacement retains its documented scope. Authored builders reproduce the shipped payloads.

No successful live drag race, wall/car test, cornering improvement, real-car dyno improvement or online race is claimed. The menu passes simulated DOM checks. The strict-CSP Chromium regression test could not run because this environment blocks Chromium startup; no real-browser visual verification is claimed.

The v0.11 crash remains undiagnosed. Controlled interleaving tests did expose stale-state and competing-writer hazards in power, grip and NOS. This release rechecks live state/identity at each field, uses exact-value atomic updates/restoration, rejects out-of-domain power values and avoids unchanged-value rewrites. These are experimental mitigations, not full lifetime synchronization: the native game can still destroy/reuse an object before updating its pointer. No elimination of that residual race or the reported freezes is claimed. The current game-thread gcall ABI, dispatch mapping and hook-local layout match the reviewed native binary; that does not establish the absence of timing, lifetime or gameplay faults. Stop using a feature if the game becomes unstable, preserve the crash log and reload before retesting.

Exact supported profiles:

- **93af6ccb:** 38,205,596 bytes, SHA-256 `128e2b5816a8eace4b768aec920318a1613da8235801a361e2009e96550be1d6`. Newest reviewed profile, with the64-entry native status table and all current controls.
- **78e2bb69:** 38,170,601 bytes, SHA-256 `df7b930bb293ffdf975f0735d93e0797d51bd137d0cbeabcaff87fc5a693c759`. Previous reviewed modern profile. Main hook 21213, dispatch 21726, gcall 21740, pace wrapper 21263, contact wrapper 22470; exact native bodies and relocated wrappers are checked offline.
- **2f0ddd3b:** 36,872,934 bytes, SHA-256 `5e33ad2cb4c4cc6893dee7cbd4d6e9bfb0f59a349d218fddbb5e3331ca69bc34`. Expanded experimental feature support listed above. The native gcall function was mapped from old index 21725 to current index 21739 and verified to preserve the same CPU ABI; actual dispatch tables and native AI bodies were checked independently.
- **6f4f1e4e:** 37,839,055 bytes, SHA-256 `ee5d281a3109240d5db25dc3921e1044672cf6d650eb58c3baa089b54fe2941f`. Retains the older combined experimental feature set.

An independent probe executes actual current-build input/status initialization, status writing and the NOS reader in isolated memory: 22 assertions pass. This verifies the mailbox formats and NOS interpretation, not a real gameplay session. A separate native gcall binary comparison verifies that its only body change is the dispatcher call relocation.

## Privacy, implementation and rollback

The extension matches only `https://nfsu2.xyz/*`. No account, history, debugger or broad website permissions. It stores its own preferences and a bounded, sanitized diagnostic history in namespaced same-tab session-storage entries. Nothing is uploaded. Its only added request is a same-origin `/game.json` compatibility read; it inspects the game's own module response during loading. No analytics, remote code or game assets are bundled.

- AI calls native `Player::AutoPilotOn`, `AutoPilotOff` and `SetInputMode` through the game's existing CPU-preserving game-thread dispatcher. It never invokes native game functions concurrently from the page thread.
- Normal drag opponents use driver type 3 / physics type 1, while player autopilot initially asks for physics type 3. The retained drag handoff corrects only the eligible local car, verifies both types and rolls back on failure.
- The page's automatic AI switch supplies the exact drag-permission word only when drag is detected. The native permission and full-physics checks are still required. The pace hook never modifies drag.
- Mode switching publishes OFF and verifies the native heartbeat acknowledgement, cleared ownership and restored manual driver before rearming. Identity, native subtype/track flags and race/free-roam mode are part of that comparison. Native Off/On rebuilds the private driver route.
- Command memory stays at `0x00d0d100` (104 bytes used on modern Drag-heat profiles;92 bytes on older profiles) and walls at `0x00d0d180` (40 bytes), under sequence locks. Cars use `0x00d0d1c0` (40 bytes); the existing final word selects the independent online traffic/player modes on 93af6ccb and 78e2bb69. The corner record is at `0x00d0d200` (64 bytes, CNR3), and dyno uses `0x00d0d300..0x00d0d4ff`. These do not overlap. Native scalar-reference/allocator analysis supports using these gaps, but exclusive allocation has not been formally proved and unknown computed writes remain a risk. Cold empty/owned checks and post-attachment ownership guards reduce, not eliminate, that risk. The current-build patch targets the main-loop bridge, player pace, contact resolver, corner/braking helpers, native drag action/input selectors, native Drift damping expression and three guarded nitrous acceptance sites. Original native instructions remain preserved around the scoped changes.
- The full tuner additionally grows the game memory by an owned 16 MiB snapshot buffer, records its module/memory identity and uses the existing dyno mailbox for commands. Snapshot growth is not undone until reload. Native evaluation runs in separate memory with guarded reads/writes and execution fuel. Staging does not call a game physics rebuild or save helper.
- Wall filtering prefixes `sub_005b2610` and preserves the full original resolver for every rejected contact. Body type/vtable, reciprocal car/face pointers, finite unit normals and pair identities are checked. Native `roam_game_online_here()` always blocks wall filtering during multiplayer free roam. The separate latest-build traffic path also calls the exact native read-only player-slot helper and excludes recognized player cars.

For rollback, disable v0.29.0, enable your preserved previous version and reload. The previous version remains subject to its own build-compatibility checks. Memory effects do not survive reload; saved ordinary preferences may. Never run both versions together.

### Tuner snapshot rejection diagnostics

A snapshot rejection keeps the original setup and remains fail-closed. Updated errors identify the failed component with a short code such as **S32** (performance-curve sample count) or **S45** (curve data bounds). Export **Crash log** immediately after one failed attempt; the local export retains only the rejection status, fixed guard code, and relevant count/source-pair number, plus ordinary classified script locations. It does not include memory addresses, raw game memory, setups, or saves.

This is a diagnostic improvement, not proof that a previously unsupported live snapshot is now compatible. Capture limits, alias checks, the owned 16 MiB buffer, isolated native evaluation, all 41 settings, and selected-preset-only Stage/Restore are unchanged. Do not disable checks or invent missing curve data to make a capture succeed.

          if(i===BRAKING.index-37){
            const fn=patchBrakingBody(bytes.subarray(fnStart,fnEnd));pieces.push(leb(fn.length),fn);changed++;
          }else if(i===CORNER.index-37){
            const fn=patchCornerBody(bytes.subarray(fnStart,fnEnd));pieces.push(leb(fn.length),fn);changed++;
          }else if(i===TARGET){
            const old=bytes.subarray(fnStart,fnEnd),a=locals(old),b=locals(BRIDGE);
            if(a.types.length!==31 || b.types.length!==64 || a.types.some((v,k)=>v!==b.types[k]) || old[old.length-1]!==11 || BRIDGE[BRIDGE.length-1]!==11)
              throw Error('Native AI hook layout changed.');
            const fn=join(BRIDGE.subarray(0,BRIDGE.length-1),old.subarray(a.end));
            pieces.push(leb(fn.length),fn);changed++;
          }else if(i===PACE_TARGET){
            const old=bytes.subarray(fnStart,fnEnd);
            if(locals(old).types.length!==1 || old[old.length-1]!==11 || PACE[PACE.length-1]!==11)
              throw Error('Native AI pace hook layout changed.');
            pieces.push(leb(PACE.length),PACE);changed++;
          }else if(i===WALL_TARGET){
            const old=bytes.subarray(fnStart,fnEnd),a=locals(old),b=locals(WALL);
            if(a.types.length!==1 || a.types[0]!==127 || b.types.length!==19 || b.types[0]!==127 || old[old.length-1]!==11 || WALL[WALL.length-1]!==11)
              throw Error('Wall contact hook layout changed.');
            const fn=join(WALL.subarray(0,WALL.length-1),old.subarray(a.end));
            pieces.push(leb(fn.length),fn);changed++;
          }else pieces.push(bytes.subarray(sizeAt,fnEnd));
          p.i=fnEnd;
        }
        if(changed!==5 || p.i!==end)throw Error('Native AI hooks were not found.');
        const section=join(...pieces);
        output=join(bytes.subarray(0,start),Uint8Array.of(10),leb(section.length),section,bytes.subarray(end));
        break;
      }
      p.i=end;
    }
    if(!output)throw Error('Native AI hook was not found.');
    return output;
  }
  function patchDragSelector(old,config) {
    const a=locals(old),off=config.offset;
    if(old.length!==config.originalLength || a.types.length!==4 || a.types.some(t=>t!==127) || old[off]!==65 || old[off+1]!==3)
      throw Error('Native drag selector layout changed.');
    // The exact module hash pins the site; preserve every other native instruction.
    return join(Uint8Array.of(1,config.locals,127),old.subarray(a.end,off),Uint8Array.from(config.expression),old.subarray(off+2));
  }
  function patchDragInputBody(old,config) {
    const a=locals(old),expected=config.originalTypes.map(t=>({i32:127,f32:125}[t]));
    if(old.length!==config.originalLength || a.types.length!==expected.length || a.types.some((t,i)=>t!==expected[i]))
      throw Error('Native drag input lifecycle layout changed.');
    return join(Uint8Array.from(config.header),Uint8Array.from(config.prefix),old.subarray(a.end));
  }
  function patchDragOverheatBody(old,config) {
    const a=locals(old),expected=config.originalTypes.map(t=>({i32:127,f32:125,f64:124}[t]));
    if(old.length!==config.originalLength || a.types.length!==expected.length || a.types.some((t,i)=>t!==expected[i]))throw Error('Native drag overheat layout changed.');
    return join(Uint8Array.from(config.header),Uint8Array.from(config.prefix),old.subarray(a.end));
  }
  function patchOwnedNosBody(old,config) {
    const a=locals(old),off=config.offset,expected=config.originalTypes.map(t=>({i32:127,f32:125,f64:124}[t]));
    if(old.length!==config.originalLength || a.types.length!==expected.length || a.types.some((t,i)=>t!==expected[i]) || old[off-3]!==65 || old[off-2]!==2 || old[off-1]!==71)
      throw Error('Native nitrous gate layout changed.');
    // Keep the original type2 comparison, then optionally accept the guarded owned player.
    return join(Uint8Array.from(config.header),old.subarray(a.end,off),Uint8Array.from(config.expression),old.subarray(off));
  }
  function patchDriftRecoveryBody(old,config) {
    const a=locals(old),off=config.offset,expected=config.originalTypes.map(t=>({i32:127,f32:125,f64:124}[t]));
    if(old.length!==config.originalLength || a.types.length!==expected.length || a.types.some((t,i)=>t!==expected[i]) || config.needle.some((v,i)=>old[off+i]!==v) || config.slice.some((v,i)=>old[config.sliceOffset+i]!==v))
      throw Error('Native drift recovery layout changed.');
    // The full-module hash pins the body. Only its player-curve expression
    // and appended authored locals change; no calls, stores or persistent undo.
    return join(Uint8Array.from(config.header),old.subarray(a.end,off),Uint8Array.from(config.expression),old.subarray(off+config.needle.length));
  }
  function patchCurrent(bytes,profile) {
    const bridge=Uint8Array.from(profile.bridge),p={i:8};
    while(p.i<bytes.length){
      const start=p.i,id=bytes[p.i++],size=read(bytes,p),begin=p.i,end=begin+size;
      if(end>bytes.length)throw Error('Invalid current module section');
      if(id===10){
        const n=read(bytes,p),pieces=[bytes.subarray(begin,p.i)];let changed=0;
        for(let i=0;i<n;i++){
          const at=p.i,len=read(bytes,p),body=p.i,stop=body+len;
          if(stop>end)throw Error('Invalid current function');
          const nos=profile.capabilities.ownedNativeNos && profile.ownedNos.find(c=>c.target===i);
          if(profile.capabilities.nativeDragOverheat && i===profile.dragOverheat.target){
            const fn=patchDragOverheatBody(bytes.subarray(body,stop),profile.dragOverheat);pieces.push(leb(fn.length),fn);changed++;
          }else if(profile.capabilities.nativeDriftRecovery && i===profile.driftRecovery.target){
            const fn=patchDriftRecoveryBody(bytes.subarray(body,stop),profile.driftRecovery);pieces.push(leb(fn.length),fn);changed++;
          }else if(nos){
            const fn=patchOwnedNosBody(bytes.subarray(body,stop),nos);pieces.push(leb(fn.length),fn);changed++;
          }else if(profile.capabilities.nativeDragInputHandoff && i===profile.dragInputGuard.target){
            const fn=patchDragInputBody(bytes.subarray(body,stop),profile.dragInputGuard);pieces.push(leb(fn.length),fn);changed++;
          }else if(profile.capabilities.opponentDrag && i===profile.dragSelector.target){
            const fn=patchDragSelector(bytes.subarray(body,stop),profile.dragSelector);pieces.push(leb(fn.length),fn);changed++;
          }else if(i===profile.target){
            const old=bytes.subarray(body,stop),a=locals(old),b=locals(bridge);
            if(a.types.length!==31||b.types.length!==profile.locals||a.types.some((v,k)=>v!==b.types[k])||old[old.length-1]!==11||bridge[bridge.length-1]!==11)throw Error('Current AI hook layout changed.');
            const fn=join(bridge.subarray(0,bridge.length-1),old.subarray(a.end));pieces.push(leb(fn.length),fn);changed++;
          }else if(profile.capabilities.pace && i===profile.pace.target){
            const old=bytes.subarray(body,stop),replacement=Uint8Array.from(profile.pace.bridge);
            if(locals(old).types.length!==1||old[old.length-1]!==11||replacement[replacement.length-1]!==11)throw Error('Current pace hook layout changed.');
            pieces.push(leb(replacement.length),replacement);changed++;
          }else if(profile.capabilities.corner && i===BRAKING.index-37){
            const fn=patchBrakingBody(bytes.subarray(body,stop));pieces.push(leb(fn.length),fn);changed++;
          }else if(profile.capabilities.corner && i===CORNER.index-37){
            const fn=patchCornerBody(bytes.subarray(body,stop));pieces.push(leb(fn.length),fn);changed++;
          }else if(profile.capabilities.walls && i===profile.wall.target){
            const old=bytes.subarray(body,stop),replacement=Uint8Array.from(profile.wall.bridge),a=locals(old),b=locals(replacement);
            if(a.types.length!==1||a.types[0]!==127||b.types.length!==19||b.types[0]!==127||old[old.length-1]!==11||replacement[replacement.length-1]!==11)throw Error('Current wall hook layout changed.');
            const fn=join(replacement.subarray(0,replacement.length-1),old.subarray(a.end));pieces.push(leb(fn.length),fn);changed++;
          }else pieces.push(bytes.subarray(at,stop));
          p.i=stop;
        }
        if(changed!==1+Number(!!profile.capabilities.nativeDragOverheat)+Number(!!profile.capabilities.nativeDragInputHandoff)+Number(!!profile.capabilities.nativeDriftRecovery)+(profile.capabilities.ownedNativeNos?profile.ownedNos.length:0)+Number(!!profile.capabilities.opponentDrag)+Number(profile.capabilities.pace)+2*Number(profile.capabilities.corner)+Number(profile.capabilities.walls)||p.i!==end)throw Error('Current AI hook was not found.');
        const section=join(...pieces);return join(bytes.subarray(0,start),Uint8Array.of(10),leb(section.length),section,bytes.subarray(end));
      }
      p.i=end;
    }
    throw Error('Current code section was not found.');
  }
  function install() {
    if(installed || typeof WebAssembly.compileStreaming!=='function')return;
    installed=true;
    const nativeStreaming=WebAssembly.compileStreaming, nativeCompile=WebAssembly.compile;
    WebAssembly.compileStreaming=async function(source,options){
      const response=await source;
      let url;try{url=new URL(response.url);}catch{return nativeStreaming.call(WebAssembly,response,options);}
      if(url.origin!==location.origin || url.pathname!=='/game.wasm')return nativeStreaming.call(WebAssembly,response,options);
      const generation=++loadGeneration,state={phase:'preparing',reason:'Preparing native AI bridge.'};
      // Concurrent loads keep independent facts; only the newest observed load publishes diagnostics.
      const publish=()=>{if(generation!==loadGeneration)return;for(const key of Object.keys(patchState))delete patchState[key];Object.assign(patchState,state);};
      publish();
      let stage='module-read';
      try{
        const bytes=await response.clone().arrayBuffer();
        state.moduleBytes=bytes.byteLength;
        const candidate=profileForSize(bytes.byteLength);
        if(candidate)state.candidateRevision=candidate.revision;
        // Read-only fingerprint coverage. It never grants compatibility or changes hooks.
        const scanner=root.__NFSU2_SIGNATURES__,references=[root.__NFSU2_SIGNATURE_PROFILE__,root.__NFSU2_SIGNATURE_PROFILE_LATEST__,root.__NFSU2_SIGNATURE_PROFILE_NEXT__].filter(Boolean);
        if(scanner?.scanAll&&references.length)try{
          const result=await scanner.scanAll(bytes,references),summary=result.bestReference;
          state.moduleHash=summary.moduleSha256;
          Object.assign(state,{signatureReference:summary.referenceRevision,signatureExact:summary.referenceModuleMatches,signatureTotal:summary.anchors,signatureUnique:summary.unique,signatureAmbiguous:summary.ambiguous,signatureMissing:summary.missing});
        }catch{state.signatureFailed=true;}
        stage='module-layout';
        let changed=await patchBytes(bytes);
        let captureInstalled=false;
        const capture=root.__NFSU2_RACE_CAPTURE__,captureProfile=profileForSize(bytes.byteLength);
        if(capture&&captureProfile?.hash===capture.PIN){
          try{const candidateBytes=await capture.patchModule(changed,captureProfile);if(!WebAssembly.validate(candidateBytes))throw Error('Capture module validation failed');changed=candidateBytes;captureInstalled=true;}
          catch{state.captureUnavailable=true;}
        }
        stage='module-compile';
        const module=await nativeCompile.call(WebAssembly,changed,options);
        const profile=profileForSize(bytes.byteLength);patched.set(module,captureInstalled?Object.freeze({...profile,capabilities:Object.freeze({...profile.capabilities,nativeRaceCapture:true})}):profile);
        if(profile.capabilities.fullTuner&&root.__NFSU2_DYNO_NATIVE__){const prepared=root.__NFSU2_DYNO_NATIVE__.build(bytes);prepared.catch(()=>{});nativeEvaluators.set(module,prepared);}
        state.phase='ready';state.revision=profile.revision;state.reason='Verified game module · native AI bridge loaded.';
        publish();return module;
      }catch(e){
        state.phase='unavailable';state.reason=String(e?.message || 'Native AI could not be prepared.');
        state.patchCode=['module-size','module-hash'].includes(e?.patchCode)?e.patchCode:stage;
        if(typeof e?.moduleHash==='string'&&/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(e.moduleHash))state.moduleHash=e.moduleHash;
        // Fail open to the unchanged game, closed to AI control. All memory-writing tools still require a verified module profile.
        publish();return nativeStreaming.call(WebAssembly,response,options);
      }
    };
  }
  class Controller {
    constructor(memory,available=false,capabilities=LEGACY.capabilities){this.memory=memory;this.available=!!available;this.capabilities=capabilities;this.hb=0;this.words=null;this.view=null;this.requestTarget=null;this.handbackPending=false;this.handbackHeartbeat=0;}
    refresh(){const b=this.memory.buffer;if(!this.view || this.view.buffer!==b){this.view=new DataView(b);this.words=new Int32Array(b);}return b.byteLength>=(this.capabilities.corner?CORNER.commandBase+64:BASE+92);}
    u32(p){return p>=0x10000 && p+4<=Math.min(this.view.byteLength,0x28000000)?this.view.getUint32(p,true):0;}
    read(off){return Atomics.load(this.words,(BASE+off)/4)>>>0;}
    write(off,v){Atomics.store(this.words,(BASE+off)/4,v|0);}
    cornerSettings(mode,pace,cornerAssist,cornerFactor,cornerMargin,raceCornerAssist,raceCornerFactor,raceCornerMargin,raceBraking,allowNetwork=false,adaptiveCorners=false){
      const raceType=this.u32(0x89e7b0),drag=!!this.view.getUint8(0x89e7d8);
      const special=drag||this.view.getUint8(0x89e7d9)||this.u32(0x890104)||this.u32(0x890108)||this.u32(0x890114);
      const network=(this.u32(0x850078)&520)||this.u32(0x866a14)||this.u32(0x8669f4)||this.view.getUint8(0x89cf69);
      const streetX=this.view.getUint8(0x89e7e3)||this.u32(0x89010c)||network&&this.u32(0x850088)===10;
      const command=!this.capabilities.corner?0:raceCornerAssist===true&&mode===1&&raceType===1&&!special&&(!network||allowNetwork===true)?adaptiveCorners===true&&this.capabilities.nativeDragInputHandoff===true&&!streetX&&Number.isFinite(pace)&&pace>=1&&pace<=2?3:2:cornerAssist===true&&mode===2&&raceType===0&&!drag?1:0;
      const factor=command>=2?raceCornerFactor:cornerFactor,sharp=command>=2?raceCornerMargin:cornerMargin;
      const percent=Number.isFinite(factor)&&factor>=.6&&factor<=.95?Math.round(factor*100):80;
      const margin=Number.isFinite(sharp)&&sharp>=0&&sharp<=25?Math.round(sharp):command>=2?15:0;
      const braking=command>=2?(Number.isFinite(raceBraking)&&raceBraking>=.5&&raceBraking<=1?Math.round(raceBraking*100):75):100;
      const pacePercent=command>=2&&this.capabilities.pace&&Number.isFinite(pace)&&pace>=.75&&pace<=3?Math.round(pace*100):100;
      return {command,percent,margin,braking,pacePercent};
    }
    nativeDriftPace() {
      return this.capabilities.nativeDriftPace===true && !this.view.getUint8(0x89e7d8) && !this.u32(0x890108) && !!(this.view.getUint8(0x89e7d9)||this.u32(0x890104)||this.u32(0x890114));
    }
    publish(wanted=0,player=0,car=0,race=0,pace=1,allowNetwork=false,allowDragAI=false,cornerAssist=false,cornerFactor=0.8,cornerMargin=0,raceCornerAssist=false,raceCornerFactor=.8,raceCornerMargin=15,raceBraking=.75,dragNoBlowout=false,adaptiveCorners=false){
      if(!this.available || !this.refresh() || this.read(28)!==MAGIC)return false;
      pace=this.capabilities.pace&&!this.nativeDriftPace()?pace:1;allowDragAI=this.capabilities.dragAI&&allowDragAI;cornerAssist=this.capabilities.corner&&cornerAssist;
      // OFF is a command the native loop must process, not merely a page
      // state. A quick same-event restart must not overwrite an unseen OFF.
      if(wanted===0 && this.read(8)!==0)this.handbackPending=true;
      let seq=this.read(4);if(seq&1)seq++;
      this.write(4,seq+1);this.write(0,MAGIC);this.write(8,wanted);this.write(12,player);this.write(16,car);this.write(20,race);
      this.write(60,Number.isFinite(pace) && pace>=0.75 && pace<=3 ? Math.round(pace*100) : 100);
      if(this.capabilities.nativeDragOverheat)this.write(100,dragNoBlowout===true?1:0);
      this.write(84,allowNetwork === true ? 1 : 0);this.write(88,allowDragAI === true ? 1 : 0);
      if(this.capabilities.corner){
      const {command,percent,margin,braking,pacePercent}=this.cornerSettings(wanted,pace,cornerAssist,cornerFactor,cornerMargin,raceCornerAssist,raceCornerFactor,raceCornerMargin,raceBraking,allowNetwork,adaptiveCorners);
      const cr=off=>Atomics.load(this.words,(CORNER.commandBase+off)/4)>>>0,cw=(off,v)=>Atomics.store(this.words,(CORNER.commandBase+off)/4,v|0);
      const cornerOwned=cr(0)===CORNER.commandMagic,cornerEmpty=Array.from({length:16},(_,i)=>cr(i*4)).every(v=>v===0);
      if(cornerOwned||cornerEmpty){
      if(cr(0)!==CORNER.commandMagic || cr(4)!==command || cr(8)!==percent || cr(36)!==margin || cr(44)!==braking || cr(48)!==pacePercent || (cr(12)&&cr(12)!==car)){
        for(let off=12;off<36;off+=4)cw(off,0);cw(40,0);cw(52,0);cw(56,0);cw(60,0);
      }
      cw(0,CORNER.commandMagic);cw(4,command);cw(8,percent);cw(36,margin);cw(44,braking);cw(48,pacePercent);}}
      this.write(24,++this.hb);this.write(4,seq+2);
      if(wanted===0 && this.handbackPending)this.handbackHeartbeat=this.hb;
      return true;
    }
    handbackObserved(){
      const current=this.status();
      // Heartbeat observation precedes processing: latch and ownership must
      // also be cleared, and the current driver must be safely manual.
      return current.ready && !current.owned && current.manual && this.read(72)===0 && this.read(44)===(this.handbackHeartbeat>>>0);
    }
    stop(){this.publish(0);return this.status();}
    releaseForSwap(){
      this.publish(0);this.handbackHeartbeat=this.hb;
      const current=this.status();
      return current.available ? {...current,switching:true,status:'switching',reason:'Changing native event behavior or corner settings · waiting for native handback.'} : current;
    }
    update({enabled=false,safe=false,state=null,mode=0,pace=1,allowNetwork=false,allowDragAI=false,cornerAssist=false,cornerFactor=0.8,cornerMargin=0,raceCornerAssist=false,raceCornerFactor=.8,raceCornerMargin=15,raceBraking=.75,dragNoBlowout=false,adaptiveCorners=false}={}){
      this.refresh();
      allowDragAI=this.capabilities.dragAI&&allowDragAI;cornerAssist=this.capabilities.corner&&cornerAssist;pace=this.capabilities.pace?pace:1;
      raceCornerAssist=this.capabilities.corner&&raceCornerAssist===true&&(!state?.network||allowNetwork===true)&&!state?.drag;
      const player=this.u32(0xd00000);
      const wanted=!!enabled && !!safe && state?.ready && state.driving && (!state.network || allowNetwork === true) && (!state.drag || allowDragAI === true) && (mode===1 || mode===2) && this.u32(player+4)===state.car;
      // A completed OFF should stop displaying as pending even while the
      // user leaves AI disabled. Do not create another handshake for idle OFF.
      if(!wanted && this.handbackPending && this.handbackObserved())this.handbackPending=false;
      // A race can change type while reusing player/car/race pointers. Never
      // retain the previous mode's physics: release our native driver first.
      // Keep the remembered target across pause/stop, so a quick re-enable or
      // transition cannot hide an unprocessed native handback request.
      if(wanted){
        const raceType=this.u32(0x89e7b0);
        const corner=this.cornerSettings(mode,pace,cornerAssist,cornerFactor,cornerMargin,raceCornerAssist,raceCornerFactor,raceCornerMargin,raceBraking,allowNetwork,adaptiveCorners);
        // Native planned caps are cached: rebuild the private route on every
        // effective corner-profile/category change, never merely reissue ON.
        // These native race parameter / forced-mode flags select or specialize
        // the game's driver. Track identity also catches a new event reusing
        // every object pointer. We request reconstruction; never fake an
        // opponent racer type or substitute an extension steering algorithm.
        const event=[this.u32(0x89e7a0),this.u32(0x89e7b4),
          ...[0x89e7d8,0x89e7d9,0x89e7e1,0x89e7e3].map(a=>this.view.getUint8(a)),
          this.u32(0x890104),this.u32(0x890108),this.u32(0x89010c),this.u32(0x890114)];
        const target=[player,state.car,state.race,state.drag?'drag':'native',mode,raceType,...event,corner.command,corner.command?corner.percent:0,corner.command?corner.margin:0,corner.command>=2?corner.braking:0,corner.command>=2?corner.pacePercent:0].join(':');
        const changed=this.requestTarget!==null && this.requestTarget!==target;
        if(changed)this.handbackPending=true;
        this.requestTarget=target;
        if(changed)return this.releaseForSwap();
        if(this.handbackPending){
          if(!this.handbackObserved())return this.releaseForSwap();
          this.handbackPending=false;
        }
      }
      this.publish(wanted?mode:0,player,state?.car||0,state?.race||0,pace,allowNetwork,allowDragAI,cornerAssist,cornerFactor,cornerMargin,raceCornerAssist,raceCornerFactor,raceCornerMargin,raceBraking,this.capabilities.nativeDragOverheat&&dragNoBlowout===true&&safe===true&&state?.ready&&state.driving&&state.drag&&(!state.network||allowNetwork===true),adaptiveCorners);
      return this.status();
    }
    status(){
      if(!this.available)return {available:false,ready:false,active:false,level:null,status:'unavailable',reason:patchState.reason==='Waiting for game module.'?'Reload the game after updating the extension.':patchState.reason};
      if(!this.refresh() || this.read(28)!==MAGIC)return {available:true,ready:false,active:false,level:null,status:'waiting',reason:'Waiting for the native game loop.'};
      const owned=this.read(36),player=this.u32(0xd00000),car=this.u32(player+4),code=this.read(52);
      const drag=!!this.view.getUint8(0x89e7d8),dragEnabled=this.read(88)===1;
      const valid=p=>p>=0x10000 && p+4096<Math.min(this.view.byteLength,0x28000000);
      const record=this.u32(car+20);
      const driftPhysicsRequired=!!this.capabilities.nativeDriftPhysics&&!drag&&!this.u32(0x890108)&&!!(this.u32(0x890114)||this.view.getUint8(0x89e7d9)||this.u32(0x890104))&&valid(record)&&this.u32(record+4)===1&&this.view.getUint8(record+0x900)===0;
      const candidateDriver=this.u32(car+44);
      const driftDriverValid=valid(candidateDriver)&&this.u32(candidateDriver)===0x785370&&this.u32(candidateDriver+4)===car;
      const dragInputOwned=!this.capabilities.nativeDragInputHandoff||!drag||(this.read(92)===1&&this.u32(player+556)===4&&this.u32(player+560)===4);
      const active=dragInputOwned&&(!driftPhysicsRequired||driftDriverValid)&&(!(drag||driftPhysicsRequired) || this.u32(car+0x28)===1) && !!owned && owned===car && this.read(32)===player && this.u32(car+0x24)===3 && code===1;
      const driver=active?this.u32(car+0x2c):0;
      const action=valid(driver)&&this.u32(driver)===0x785370&&this.u32(driver+4)===car?this.u32(driver+0x6fc):0;
      const actionId=valid(action)?this.u32(action+20):null;
      const opponentDragSelected=active&&drag&&actionId===2&&this.u32(action)===0x7847d0;

    if (state.cornerProbeStage >= 1 && state.cornerProbeStage <= 4) return 'Armed · native corner checks not yet complete';
    return 'Armed · no native corner reduction recorded';
  }
  function cornerEvidenceText(state) {
    const count = value => Number.isInteger(value) && value >= 0 && value <= 40 ? value : 'unknown';
    const stage = Number.isInteger(state.cornerProbeStage) && state.cornerProbeStage >= 0 && state.cornerProbeStage <= 7 ? state.cornerProbeStage : 'unknown';
    const mask = Number.isInteger(state.cornerGuardMask) && state.cornerGuardMask >= 0 && state.cornerGuardMask <= 255 ? state.cornerGuardMask : null;
    const checks = [[1,'command/profile'],[2,'AI ownership'],[4,'game context'],[8,'race state'],[16,'drag/drift exclusion'],[32,'network permission'],[64,'driver identity'],[128,'private route']];
    const sampled = mask === null ? 'unknown' : mask ? checks.filter(([bit]) => mask & bit).map(([,name]) => name).join(', ') : 'none';
    return `Native route points: ${count(state.cornerRouteNodes)}; corner entries: ${count(state.cornerPlannerCorners)}. Furthest native check: ${stage}/7; 7 means a hit exists. Sampled unmet checks: ${sampled}. Counts/checks are snapshots, not a proven cause. Export a short crash log after several turns if no reduction is recorded.`;
  }
  const NativeWorker = window.Worker;
  // Observe only the known game worker; AI validates its patched module separately.
  window.Worker = new Proxy(NativeWorker, {
    construct(Target, args, NewTarget) {
      const worker = Reflect.construct(Target, args, NewTarget);
      let url; try { url = new URL(String(args[0]), location.href); } catch { return worker; }
      if (url.origin !== location.origin || url.pathname !== '/host/game-worker.js') return worker;
      const send = worker.postMessage;
      let bootSession=null;
      worker.postMessage = function (m, ...rest) {
        if (m && m.mod instanceof WebAssembly.Module && m.memory instanceof WebAssembly.Memory && Number.isSafeInteger(m.slot) && m.slot>=0) {
          if(m.slot===0){
          const verifiedProfile=AI?.getModuleProfile?.(m.mod)||null;
          if (!engine || engine.memory !== m.memory || activeModule!==m.mod || activeWorker!==worker || moduleProfile!==verifiedProfile) {
            // Release only the previous verified session before sending the new
            // module to its worker. A reused memory object is not an identity.
            if(engine&&moduleProfile){try{const state=engine.state();engine.restorePerformance(state);engine.restoreGrip(state);}catch{}}
            dyno?.cancel();wall?.stop();cars?.stop();ai?.stop();
            sessionGeneration++;activeWorker=worker;activeModule=m.mod;moduleProfile=verifiedProfile;refreshCompatibility();
            // A new module/worker/memory generation has no current native
            // observations yet. Do not carry prior application or ownership
            // evidence into its boot event or an immediate diagnostic export.
            diagnosticState={generation:sessionGeneration,revision:moduleProfile?.revision||'unknown',supported,ready:false,driving:false,safe:false,tools:diagnosticTools()};
            clearApplicationEvidence('not-ready');
            diagnosticIdentity=null;
            recordDiagnostic('game-boot',{generation:sessionGeneration,slot:m.slot,memoryMiB:m.memory.buffer.byteLength/1048576,revision:moduleProfile?.revision||'unknown',supported,tools:diagnosticTools()});
            const caps=moduleProfile?.capabilities;
            dyno=caps?.fullTuner && globalThis.__NFSU2_DYNO_FULL__?.Controller?new globalThis.__NFSU2_DYNO_FULL__.Controller(m.memory,true,moduleProfile.revision,{prepared:AI.getNativeEvaluator(m.mod),module:m.mod}):caps?.dyno && globalThis.__NFSU2_DYNO__?.Controller?new globalThis.__NFSU2_DYNO__.Controller(m.memory,true,moduleProfile.revision):null;dyno?.setEnabled(dynoEnabled);
            wall=caps?.walls && Walls?.Controller?new Walls.Controller(m.memory,true,moduleProfile.wall):null;
            cars=caps?.cars && Cars?.Controller?new Cars.Controller(m.memory,true,moduleProfile.cars):null;
            ai=AI?.Controller?new AI.Controller(m.memory,!!caps?.ai,caps):null;
            raceCapture?.stop('Game session changed');raceCapture=caps?.nativeRaceCapture&&globalThis.__NFSU2_RACE_CAPTURE__?.Controller?new globalThis.__NFSU2_RACE_CAPTURE__.Controller(m.memory,true,m.mod):null;updateRaceCapture();
            engine = new Engine(m.memory,moduleProfile?.statusCapacity); statusPtr = 0; inputPtr = 0; driftPending = null; driftNeedsReapply=typeof prefs.drift==='boolean'; powerGate.reset(); gripGate.reset();
          }
          }
          bootSession={module:m.mod,memory:m.memory,generation:activeModule===m.mod&&engine?.memory===m.memory?sessionGeneration:-1};
        }
        return Reflect.apply(send, this, [m, ...rest]);
      };
      const currentSession = () => !!bootSession && bootSession.generation===sessionGeneration && bootSession.module===activeModule && bootSession.memory===engine?.memory;
      worker.addEventListener('error', event => recordDiagnostic('worker-error',{sessionCurrent:currentSession(),error:event.error || event.message,tools:diagnosticTools()}));
      worker.addEventListener('message', event => {
        const m = event.data;
        if(m?.t==='trap')recordDiagnostic('game-trap',{sessionCurrent:currentSession(),tid:m.tid,error:m.msg,stack:m.stack,tools:diagnosticTools()});
        if(m?.t==='exit')recordDiagnostic('game-exit',{sessionCurrent:currentSession(),code:m.code,tools:diagnosticTools()});
        if(!currentSession())return;
        if(m?.t==='register' && (m.kind===3||m.kind===5))recordDiagnostic('game-register',{kind:m.kind});
        if (worker===activeWorker && m?.t === 'register' && m.kind === 3 && Number.isSafeInteger(m.ptr)) inputPtr = m.ptr;
        if (worker===activeWorker && m?.t === 'register' && m.kind === 5 && Number.isSafeInteger(m.ptr)) statusPtr = m.ptr;
        if (m?.t === 'exit' || m?.t === 'trap') {raceCapture?.invalidate('Recording stopped · game ended');updateRaceCapture();suspend('Game stopped. Enabled choices are kept for the next game.');ai=null;wall=null;cars=null;dyno=null;engine=null;activeWorker=null;activeModule=null;moduleProfile=null;refreshCompatibility();statusPtr=0;inputPtr=0;}
      });
      return worker;
    }
  });
  // A different game revision must be reviewed before writing its memory.
  fetch('/game.json', { cache: 'no-store', credentials: 'omit' }).then(r => {
    if (!r.ok) throw new Error('Build information unavailable');

  function key(code, down) {
    const keyName = { ArrowUp: 'ArrowUp', ShiftLeft: 'Shift', AltLeft: 'Alt' }[code] || code;
    window.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent(down ? 'keydown' : 'keyup', { code, key: keyName,
      location: /Left$/.test(code) ? 1 : 0, bubbles: true, cancelable: true }));
  }
  function hold(code, down) {
    if (down && !held.has(code)) { if (!physicallyHeld.has(code)) { held.add(code); key(code, true); } }
    else if (!down && held.delete(code) && !physicallyHeld.has(code)) key(code, false);
  }
  function release() { clearTimeout(shiftTimer); for (const code of [...held]) hold(code, false); }
  function suspend(why) {
    raceCapture?.stop('Recording stopped · tools paused');updateRaceCapture();
    dyno?.cancel();
    wall?.stop();cars?.stop(); ai?.stop(); release(); powerGate.reset(); gripGate.reset();
    try {if(engine){const state=engine.state();engine.restorePerformance(state);engine.restoreGrip(state);}} catch { /* no stale pointer writes */ }
    clearApplicationEvidence();
    if(why) message(why);
  }
  function stop(why = 'Driving controls off. F9 cleared driving assists and network permission. Saved profiles are kept. Load one manually, or select it and enable Load on startup to resume.', persistProfilePause=true) {
    raceCapture?.stop('Recording stopped · Stop pressed');updateRaceCapture();
    profileStartup=null;loadedProfile=null;profileActionEpoch++;profileActionPending=false;if(profileDriftChoice)driftNeedsReapply=false;profileDriftChoice=false;
    // Keep an already-issued drift request pending until confirmation/timeout: a
    // native toggle cannot be recalled safely, and a second must not overlap it.
    if(persistProfilePause){
      profileSessionStopped=true;
      try{sessionStorage.setItem(PROFILE_SESSION_STOP,'1');}catch{}
      const result=profileStore?.pause();
      profileNotice=result?.error||'Automatic loading paused by Stop. Select a profile and enable Load on startup to resume.';
      renderProfiles();
    }
    recordDiagnostic('stop',{tools:diagnosticTools()});
    clearRaceOnlyAI();
    dynoEnabled=false;dyno?.setEnabled(false);if(ui)ui.querySelector('#dyno-enable').checked=false;
    adaptiveRaceEnabled=false;if(ui)ui.querySelector('#adaptive-race').checked=false;
    prefs.raceCornerAssist=false;prefs.cornerAssist=false;prefs.racePace=false;prefs.walls=false;prefs.cars=false;prefs.traffic=false;prefs.players=false;prefs.online=false;prefs.ai=false;prefs.aiPace=false;prefs.nos=false;prefs.dragNoBlowout=false;prefs.drag=false;prefs.boost=false;prefs.unlimit=false;prefs.grip=false;savePrefs();suspend();
    if(ui) for(const id of ['race-corner-assist','corner-assist','race-pace','walls','cars','traffic','players','online','ai','ai-pace','nos','drag-no-blowout','drag','boost','unlimit','grip']) ui.querySelector('#'+id).checked=false;
    message(profileNotice&&persistProfilePause ? why+' '+profileNotice : why);
  }

  function raceOnlyRaceContext() {
    // Manual driving in free roam should not cancel arming for the next race.
    // Read the current context so an old sample cannot ignore race takeover.
    if(!supported||!engine||!statusPtr)return false;

  }

  }
  window.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
    if (!e.isTrusted) return;
    if(e.code==='Insert' && e.shiftKey && !e.ctrlKey && !e.altKey && !e.metaKey){
      // Shift+Insert remains Paste in text/editable controls, including controls
      // inside a shadow root. Otherwise it mirrors the existing F8 menu action.
      const path=e.composedPath?.()||[e.target];
      const editingNode=node=>{
        for(let depth=0;node&&depth<32;depth++,node=node.parentElement){
          if(node.isContentEditable || node.getAttribute?.('role')==='textbox' || /^(TEXTAREA|SELECT)$/.test(node.tagName) || (node.tagName==='INPUT' && !/^(button|checkbox|radio|range|submit|reset|color|file|image|hidden)$/.test(String(node.type||'').toLowerCase())))return true;
        }
        return false;
      };
      // Window's composedPath hides our closed shadow tree. Its retained
      // activeElement is required to preserve Paste in the profile-name field.
      const editing=[...path,ui?.activeElement,document.activeElement].some(editingNode);
      if(e.isComposing || e.defaultPrevented || editing)return;
      e.preventDefault();if(!e.repeat)setPanel(!visible);return;
    }
    // Range controls keep their native arrow/Space behavior without taking over the car.
    if(host && e.composedPath?.().includes(host) && !['F6','F7','F8','F9','Escape'].includes(e.code)) return;
    if(e.code==='F6'){e.preventDefault();if(!e.repeat)setInfoHud(!infoHudEnabled);return;}

    if (e.code === 'F8') { e.preventDefault(); setPanel(!visible); }
    if (e.code === 'Escape' && visible) setPanel(false);

  }, true);

  function setDrift(wanted) {
    if (driftPending) return false;
    const state = engine?.state(), counters = engine && statusPtr ? engine.status(statusPtr) : null;
    if (!supported || !state?.ready || !state.driving || state.network || !counters || (counters.drive & 3) !== 2 || !Number.isFinite(counters.drift) || document.hidden || document.querySelector('dialog[open]')) {
      message('Drift assist only works while driving solo free roam with the game menus closed.'); return false;
    }
    if (!!(counters.drift & 1) === wanted) return true;
    // Rebuilding the native drift setup must not inherit our power multiplier.
    engine.restorePerformance(state);engine.restoreGrip(state);powerGate.reset();gripGate.reset();
    if (!engine.driftTap(inputPtr)) { message('Drift request not sent: the game input mailbox is unavailable, inactive, typing, or full.'); return false; }
    driftPending = { wanted, until: performance.now() + 3000 };
    ui.querySelector('#drift').disabled = true;
    message('Drift request sent. Waiting for the game to confirm its handling state…');
    return true;
  }
  function moduleFailure() {
    const patch=AI?.patchState;
    if(moduleProfile || patch?.phase!=='unavailable')return '';
    const reported=/^[a-f0-9]{8,40}$/.test(revision)?` Site reports build ${revision}.`:'';
    const bytes=Number.isSafeInteger(patch.moduleBytes)?` Loaded module: ${patch.moduleBytes} bytes.`:'';
    const signatures=Number.isInteger(patch.signatureUnique)?` Fingerprints: ${patch.signatureUnique}/${patch.signatureTotal} unique matches; this does not approve an unknown build.`:'';
    return ['module-size','module-hash'].includes(patch.patchCode)
      ? `Game module is not verified.${reported}${bytes} A compatible Driving Tools update is required.${signatures}`
      : `Game module could not be prepared.${reported} Reload once. If it persists, export the diagnostic log.`;
  }
  function tick() {
    if(raceCapture){if(document.hidden||!document.hasFocus())raceCapture.stop('Recording stopped · tab inactive');else raceCapture.poll();updateRaceCapture();}
    try {
      const patch=AI?.patchState,phase=patch?.phase || 'idle';
      const key=JSON.stringify([phase,patch?.revision,patch?.moduleBytes,patch?.moduleHash,patch?.patchCode,patch?.signatureReference,patch?.signatureUnique,patch?.signatureFailed,revision]);
      if(key!==diagnosticPatch){diagnosticPatch=key;recordDiagnostic('patch-state',{phase,revision:patch?.revision,reportedRevision:revision,candidateRevision:patch?.candidateRevision,moduleBytes:patch?.moduleBytes,moduleHash:patch?.moduleHash,patchCode:patch?.patchCode,signatureReference:patch?.signatureReference,signatureExact:patch?.signatureExact,signatureTotal:patch?.signatureTotal,signatureUnique:patch?.signatureUnique,signatureMissing:patch?.signatureMissing,signatureAmbiguous:patch?.signatureAmbiguous,signatureFailed:patch?.signatureFailed,error:phase==='unavailable'?patch?.reason:undefined});}
      if(ui){const status=diagnostics?.status();ui.querySelector('#diagnostic-state').textContent=status?`${status.events} recent events · ${status.persistence==='same-tab'?'kept across reloads in this tab':'memory only; storage unavailable'}`:'Logger unavailable';if(status&&Number.isInteger(patch?.signatureUnique))ui.querySelector('#diagnostic-state').textContent+=` · fingerprints ${patch.signatureUnique}/${patch.signatureTotal}`;}
    } catch {}

      const paceConfirmed=!!aiRequested && safe && !ai?.handbackPending && !aiState.switching && !!aiState.active && Number.isFinite(aiState.paceApplied) && aiState.paceApplied>=.75 && aiState.paceApplied<=3;

      let tune={active:false},grip={active:false};

      if(safe && !driftPending && (prefs.boost || prefs.unlimit)) {
        const info=engine.performanceInfo(s),patch=engine.performancePatch;
        if(patch && (!info || patch.car!==s.car || patch.race!==s.race || patch.pi!==info.pi)) {engine.restorePerformance(s);powerGate.reset();}
        if(!info){powerGate.reset();powerStatus='layout';}
