  function setPanel(open) {
    visible=!!open;
    if(host)host.style.width=visible?'244px':'170px';
    if(!visible && dyno?.busy)dyno.cancel();
    if(!ui) return;
    ui.querySelector('#tools-panel').hidden=!visible;
    ui.querySelector('#min').setAttribute('aria-expanded',String(visible));
    ui.querySelector('#chevron').textContent=visible ? '▴' : '▾';
    renderInfoHud();
  }
  function updateDynoUI() {
    if(!ui)return;
    const busy=!!dyno?.busy,ready=!!(dynoEnabled && supported && dyno?.canUse() && !document.hidden && document.hasFocus());
    const context=ready&&!busy?dyno?.syncContext?.():null;
    if(context?.invalidated)dynoText='Car tuning or installed parts changed. Load settings or find a new tune for this game mode.';
    else if(context?.changed)dynoText=dyno.applied?'Applied tune found for this car and mode. Restore is available while it stays unchanged.':dyno.outcome?'Preview found for this car and mode. Review it before Apply.':'Ready for the selected mode. Load all settings or search a measured native estimate.';
    ui.querySelector('#dyno-mode').textContent=context?`Game tuning slot ${context.kind+1} of 5${Tune?.MODE_LABELS?.[context.kind]?' · '+Tune.MODE_LABELS[context.kind]:''} · selected in Mode Select`:busy&&dyno?.context?`Game tuning slot ${dyno.context.kind+1} of 5`:'Choose a race mode in the game, then open the Dyno main screen.';
    ui.querySelector('#dyno-find').disabled=!ready || busy || !!dyno?.applied;
    ui.querySelector('#dyno-cancel').disabled=!busy;
    ui.querySelector('#dyno-apply').disabled=!ready || busy || !(dyno?.full?dyno.outcome?.changed:dyno?.outcome?.improved) || !!dyno?.applied;
    ui.querySelector('#dyno-restore').disabled=!ready || busy || !dyno?.applied;
    ui.querySelector('#dyno-goal').disabled=busy;
    for(const option of ui.querySelector('#dyno-goal').options||[])if(['acceleration60','acceleration100','topSpeed'].includes(option.value))option.disabled=!dyno?.full;
    if(dyno && !dyno.full&&['acceleration60','acceleration100','topSpeed'].includes(ui.querySelector('#dyno-goal').value))ui.querySelector('#dyno-goal').value='peakPower';
    updateSetupEditor(ready,busy);
    ui.querySelector('#dyno-state').textContent=moduleFailure()?`Dyno unavailable. ${moduleFailure()}`:moduleProfile&&!moduleProfile.capabilities.dyno?'Not yet verified for this build':dynoText;
  }
  const tuneValue=value=>(value>100?'+':'')+(value-100);
  function updateSetupEditor(ready,busy){
    const editor=dyno?.editor,editable=!!(ready&&!busy&&editor&&!dyno?.applied);
    ui.querySelector('#tune-load').disabled=!ready||busy||!!dyno?.applied||!dyno?.full;
    ui.querySelector('#tune-preview').disabled=!editable;
    ui.querySelector('#tune-reset').disabled=!editable;
    ui.querySelector('#tune-group').disabled=!editable;
    const group=Tune?.GROUPS?.find(g=>g.id===ui.querySelector('#tune-group').value)||Tune?.GROUPS?.[0];
    for(let i=0;i<9;i++){
      const offset=group?.offsets[i],present=!!editor&&offset!==undefined,row=ui.querySelector('#tune-row-'+i),input=ui.querySelector('#tune-input-'+i);
      row.hidden=!present;input.disabled=!editable||!editor?.allowedOffsets.includes(offset);
      if(present){
        input.dataset.offset=String(offset);input.value=editor.draft[offset]-100;
        ui.querySelector('#tune-label-'+i).textContent=(Tune?.FIELD_LABELS?.[offset]||'Setting '+(offset+1))+(editor.allowedOffsets.includes(offset)?'':editor.unlockedOffsets?.includes(offset)?' · unverified':' · locked');
        ui.querySelector('#tune-value-'+i).textContent=tuneValue(editor.draft[offset]);
      }
    }
    const o=dyno?.outcome;
    ui.querySelector('#tune-changes').textContent=dyno?.full&&Array.isArray(o?.changes)?o.changes.map(x=>`${Tune?.FIELD_LABELS?.[x.offset]||x.field}: ${tuneValue(x.before)} → ${tuneValue(x.after)}${x.adjusted?' (native adjusted request '+tuneValue(x.requested)+')':''}`).join('\n')||'No accepted setup changes.':editor?'Edit sliders, then Preview changes. Drafts never alter the game.':'Load settings to see unlocked controls for this car and preset.';
  }
  async function runDyno(action) {
    if(!dynoEnabled || !dyno || dyno.busy)return;
    recordDiagnostic('dyno-action',{reason:action,tools:diagnosticTools()});
    suspend();
    dyno.setEnabled(true);
    try {
      if(action==='load'){
        await dyno.loadSetup();dynoText='All supported settings loaded. Edit a category, then Preview. Nothing changes in the game until Stage.';
      } else if(action==='preview'){
        const r=await dyno.preview();
        dynoText=`${r.changed?'Preview ready. Review accepted changes, then Stage selected preset.':'No accepted setup changes.'} Game unchanged. Native estimates: 0–60 ${r.bestResult.zeroTo60Seconds.toFixed(2)} s; 0–100 ${r.bestResult.zeroTo100Seconds.toFixed(2)} s; top ${(r.bestResult.topSpeedMps*3.6).toFixed(1)} km/h; ${r.bestResult.peakPowerKw.toFixed(1)} kW / ${r.bestResult.peakTorqueNm.toFixed(1)} Nm. NOS ${r.bestResult.nitrousSeconds.toFixed(2)} s / torque setting ${r.bestResult.nitrousTorque.toFixed(3)}. No handling/lap-time measurement.`;
      } else if(action==='find') {
        dynoText=dyno.full?'Searching in private memory · game setup stays unchanged':'Searching · original setup is restored after each trial';updateDynoUI();
        const r=await dyno.find({goal:ui.querySelector('#dyno-goal').value,onProgress:p=>{dynoText=`Searching ${p.evaluations}/${p.budget} trials · Cancel or F9 to stop`;updateDynoUI();}});
        const [field,unit]=({peakPower:['peakPowerKw','kW'],peakTorque:['peakTorqueNm','Nm'],acceleration60:['zeroTo60Seconds','s (0–60)'],acceleration100:['zeroTo100Seconds','s (0–100)'],topSpeed:['topSpeedMps','m/s']}[r.goal]);
        if(dyno.full){
          const manualSeed=r.seed?.some((value,index)=>value!==r.baseline[index]);
          const seedText=manualSeed&&r.changed?(r.improvedFromSeed?' Search improved the measured goal over your draft.':' No further measured improvement over the draft. Accepted manual draft retained.'):'';
          dynoText=`${r.baselineResult[field].toFixed(1)} → ${r.bestResult[field].toFixed(1)} ${unit} · ${r.evaluations} trials. Original kept. ${r.improved?'Measured goal improved versus original.':'No measured goal improvement versus original.'}${seedText} ${r.changed?'Review accepted changes, then Stage selected preset.':'No accepted setup changes.'} No handling/lap-time measurement.`;
        }else dynoText=`${r.baselineResult[field].toFixed(1)} → ${r.bestResult[field].toFixed(1)} ${unit} · ${r.evaluations} trials. Original kept. ${r.improved?'Stage preview to use this tune.':'No improvement found.'}`;
      } else if(action==='apply') {const r=await dyno.apply();dynoText=dyno.full?'Selected preset staged. Use the game’s Test Run to refresh driving physics, and Save Profile to persist. Disk save is not confirmed.'+(r.saveReady?'':' Other presets also have unsaved edits; native Save Profile saves them too.'):'Best tune applied. Use native Save Profile to persist.';}
      else {await dyno.restore();dynoText=dyno.full?'Previous current and selected-visit settings restored. Test Run refreshes physics. Save Profile again if you want this restored version persisted.':'Previous tune restored and confirmed.';}
    } catch(error) {recordDiagnostic('dyno-error',{error,dynoStatus:error?.dynoStatus,dynoGuard:error?.dynoGuard,dynoObserved:error?.dynoObserved,tools:diagnosticTools()});dynoText=error?.message || 'Dyno tuner stopped. Reload before retrying.';}
    updateDynoUI();
  }
  function exportDiagnostic() {
    if(!diagnostics){message('Diagnostic logger is unavailable. The game’s Download log may still have crash details.');return;}
    let url=null,link=null;
    try {
      recordDiagnostic('export',{tools:diagnosticTools()});
      const blob=new Blob([diagnostics.exportText()],{type:'application/json'});
      url=URL.createObjectURL(blob);link=document.createElement('a');link.href=url;link.download='nfsu2-driving-tools-diagnostics.json';link.hidden=true;
      (document.body||document.documentElement).append(link);link.click();
      message('Diagnostic download requested. It stays local until you choose to share the file. For native crash details, also use the game’s Download log.');
    } catch(error) {recordDiagnostic('engine-error',{error});message('Diagnostic download failed. Try again, or use the game’s Download log.');}
    finally {link?.remove();if(url)setTimeout(()=>URL.revokeObjectURL(url),1000);}
  }
  const profileToggleIds={raceCornerAssist:'race-corner-assist',cornerAssist:'corner-assist',racePace:'race-pace',walls:'walls',cars:'cars',traffic:'traffic',players:'players',online:'online',ai:'ai',aiPace:'ai-pace',nos:'nos',dragNoBlowout:'drag-no-blowout',drag:'drag',tester:'tester',boost:'boost',unlimit:'unlimit',grip:'grip'};
  const profileNumericBindings=[['race-corner-factor','raceCornerFactor','race-corner-value',2,'×'],['race-corner-margin','raceCornerMargin','race-corner-margin-value',0,'%'],['race-braking','raceBraking','race-braking-value',2,'×'],['race-pace-factor','racePaceFactor','race-pace-value',2,'×'],['corner-factor','cornerFactor','corner-value',2,'×'],['corner-margin','cornerMargin','corner-margin-value',0,'%'],['pace-factor','paceFactor','pace-value',2,'×'],['rpm','rpm','rpm-value',0,''],['power','power','power-value',1,'×'],['grip-factor','gripFactor','grip-value',1,'×']];
  function syncProfileControls(){
    if(!ui)return;
    for(const [key,id]of Object.entries(profileToggleIds))ui.querySelector('#'+id).checked=prefs[key];
    for(const [id,key,out,digits,suffix]of profileNumericBindings){const el=ui.querySelector('#'+id);el.value=prefs[key];ui.querySelector('#'+out).textContent=prefs[key].toFixed(digits)+suffix;el.setAttribute('aria-valuetext',prefs[key].toFixed(digits)+(suffix==='%'?' percent':suffix?' times':' RPM'));}
    ui.querySelector('#dyno-enable').checked=dynoEnabled;
    ui.querySelector('#drift').checked=!!prefs.drift;
    ui.querySelector('#hazards').hidden=!prefs.tester;
  }
  const profileLocks=()=>typeof navigator!=='undefined'&&navigator.locks&&typeof navigator.locks.request==='function'?navigator.locks:null;
  function renderProfiles(){
    if(!ui)return;
    const state=profileStore?.snapshot(),select=ui.querySelector('#profile-select');
    select.replaceChildren();const empty=document.createElement('option');empty.value='';empty.textContent='Choose a saved profile';select.append(empty);
    for(const p of state?.data.profiles||[]){const option=document.createElement('option');option.value=p.id;option.textContent=p.name;select.append(option);}
    const selected=state?.data.profiles.find(p=>p.id===profileSelection?.id&&p.revision===profileSelection?.revision);
    if(!selected){profileSelection=null;ui.querySelector('#profile-network').checked=false;}
    select.value=selected?.id||'';
    for(const id of ['profile-load','profile-update','profile-delete','profile-auto'])ui.querySelector('#'+id).disabled=profileActionPending||!state?.available||!selected||(id!=='profile-load'&&!profileLocks());
    ui.querySelector('#profile-save').disabled=profileActionPending||!state?.available||!profileLocks();
    for(const id of ['profile-select','profile-name','profile-network'])ui.querySelector('#'+id).disabled=profileActionPending;
    ui.querySelector('#profile-auto').checked=!!selected&&state.data.auto?.id===selected.id&&state.data.auto.stopToken===state.stopToken&&!profileSessionStopped;
    ui.querySelector('#profile-state').textContent=state?.error||(profileActionPending?'Waiting for another tab to finish saving profiles.':profileNotice)||(!profileLocks()?'Profile editing is unavailable because this browser cannot lock local saves.':!profileStore?'Profiles unavailable; existing controls still work.':state.paused?'Automatic loading paused by Stop. Save current controls, then select and Load when needed.');
  }
  function selectProfile(){
    const id=ui.querySelector('#profile-select').value,state=profileStore?.refresh();
    profileSelection=state?.data.profiles.find(p=>p.id===id)||null;
    ui.querySelector('#profile-name').value=profileSelection?.name||'';
    ui.querySelector('#profile-network').checked=profileSelection?.networkConsent||false;
    profileNotice=profileSelection?'Selected '+profileSelection.name+'. Load applies its saved choices. Update replaces it with current controls.':'';renderProfiles();
  }
  function applyToolProfile(result,automatic=false){
    if(driftPending)throw Error('Wait for the current drift request to confirm or time out, then Load again. No profile was loaded.');
    if(dyno?.busy||dyno?.pending){dyno.cancel();throw Error('Tuner cancellation requested. Wait for the pending game request to finish, then Load again. A staged preset is not reverted.');}
    clearRaceOnlyAI();
    adaptiveRaceEnabled=false;if(ui)ui.querySelector('#adaptive-race').checked=false;
    suspend();driftNeedsReapply=false;dragTakenOver=false;lastShift=0;lastPulse=0;
    const choices=result.settings;
    for(const key of Object.keys(prefs))prefs[key]=choices[key];
    dynoEnabled=choices.dynoEnabled;dyno?.setEnabled(dynoEnabled);
    if(ui){ui.querySelector('#dyno-goal').value=choices.dynoGoal;ui.querySelector('#profile-network').checked=result.profile.networkConsent;ui.querySelector('#profile-name').value=result.profile.name;}
    driftNeedsReapply=typeof prefs.drift==='boolean';profileDriftChoice=driftNeedsReapply;
    loadedProfile={id:result.profile.id,revision:result.profile.revision};savePrefs();syncProfileControls();
    dynoText=dynoEnabled?'Profile loaded. Open the solo Performance Tuning main screen. Existing staged presets are unchanged.':'Tuner off. Existing staged presets are unchanged.';updateDynoUI();
    profileNotice=(automatic?'Loaded on startup: ':'Loaded: ')+result.profile.name+'. Choices wait for verified game contexts.'+(result.profile.networkConsent?' Saved network permission restored where selected.':' Network permission and online no-clip remain off.')+' Game presets and drafts are not saved or restored by profiles.';
    message(profileNotice);renderProfiles();
  }
  function profileAction(action){
    if(profileActionPending)return;
    const request={stopToken:profileStore?.snapshot().stopToken,selection:profileSelection?{...profileSelection}:null,name:ui.querySelector('#profile-name').value,networkConsent:ui.querySelector('#profile-network').checked===true,auto:ui.querySelector('#profile-auto').checked,settings:{...prefs,dynoEnabled,dynoGoal:ui.querySelector('#dyno-goal').value}};
    const epoch=profileActionEpoch;
    // localStorage has no atomic compare-and-swap. Serialize named-profile
    // writes across tabs with a browser-managed lock; Stop remains immediate
    // and its independent marker invalidates any stale startup authorization.
    const execute=()=>{
      if(epoch!==profileActionEpoch)return;
      if(action==='auto'){
        const latest=profileStore?.refresh();
        if(!latest?.available||latest.stopToken!==request.stopToken){profileNotice='Stop or profile storage changed while waiting. Select a profile and request startup loading again.';renderProfiles();return;}
      }
      performProfileAction(action,request);
    };
    if(action==='load'){execute();return;}
    const locks=profileLocks();
    if(!locks){profileNotice='Profile editing needs browser storage locking, which is unavailable. No profile was changed.';renderProfiles();return;}
    profileActionPending=true;renderProfiles();
    try{
      const result=locks.request('nfsu2-driving-tools-profiles-v1-write',execute);
      if(result&&typeof result.then==='function')result.catch(()=>{if(epoch===profileActionEpoch)profileNotice='Could not lock profile storage. No profile change was confirmed.';}).finally(()=>{if(epoch===profileActionEpoch){profileActionPending=false;renderProfiles();}});
      else {profileActionPending=false;renderProfiles();}
    }catch{profileActionPending=false;profileNotice='Could not lock profile storage. No profile change was confirmed.';renderProfiles();}
  }
  function performProfileAction(action,request){
    const selected=request.selection;
    try{
      if(!profileStore)throw Error('Profiles are unavailable.');
      if(action==='save'||action==='update'){
        if(action==='update'&&!selected)throw Error('Select a saved profile first.');
        const saved=profileStore.save({id:action==='update'?selected.id:null,revision:action==='update'?selected.revision:null,name:request.name,settings:request.settings,networkConsent:request.networkConsent});
        profileSelection=saved;profileNotice='Saved '+saved.name+' locally in this browser. This profile will not load on startup until explicitly enabled.';
      }else if(action==='load'){
        if(!selected)throw Error('Select a saved profile first.');
        applyToolProfile(profileStore.load(selected.id,selected.revision));return;
      }else if(action==='delete'){
        if(!selected)throw Error('Select a saved profile first.');
        profileStore.remove(selected.id,selected.revision);profileSelection=null;ui.querySelector('#profile-name').value='';ui.querySelector('#profile-network').checked=false;profileNotice='Saved profile deleted. Current controls are unchanged; automatic loading for it is off.';
      }else if(action==='auto'){
        const enabled=request.auto;
        if(enabled&&!selected)throw Error('Select a saved profile first.');
        profileStore.setAuto(enabled?selected.id:null,enabled?selected.revision:null);
        if(enabled){
          // Clear the fallback latch only AFTER the requested saved revision was
          // authorized successfully; a stale/failed enable must not erase Stop.
          try{sessionStorage.removeItem(PROFILE_SESSION_STOP);if(sessionStorage.getItem(PROFILE_SESSION_STOP)==='1')throw Error();}
          catch{try{profileStore.setAuto(null);}catch{}throw Error('Cannot clear the Stop pause in this tab. Automatic loading remains blocked here; check storage before retrying.');}
          profileSessionStopped=false;
        }
        profileNotice=enabled?'Load on startup enabled for '+selected.name+'. Its saved choices, including separately saved network permission, will be requested after reload. F9 pauses this.':'Automatic profile loading is off. Current controls are unchanged.';
      }
    }catch(error){profileNotice=error.message||'Profile action failed. Nothing was loaded.';message(profileNotice);}
    renderProfiles();
  }

function triple(a,b,c){

 // requiring any one polyline vertex to turn 75 degrees. Unknown edges and
 // reversals of turn direction break the run. A long straight also breaks it.
 const runs=[];let run=null,pendingStraight=0;
 const finish=()=>{if(run){run.safetyPriority=run.angleDegrees>=thresholdDegrees-1e-6;runs.push(run);}run=null;pendingStraight=0;};
 for(const corner of corners){
  if(corner.status!=='measured'){finish();continue;}
  const sign=Math.sign(corner.signedAngleDegrees);
  if(corner.angleDegrees<1e-5){pendingStraight+=edges[corner.index]?.length||0;if(pendingStraight>maxStraightGap)finish();continue;}
  if(run&&sign!==run.sign)finish();
  if(!run)run={startIndex:corner.index,endIndex:corner.index,angleDegrees:0,sign,peakCurvature:0,indices:[],reversal:false};
  run.endIndex=corner.index;run.indices.push(corner.index);run.angleDegrees+=corner.angleDegrees;
  run.peakCurvature=Math.max(run.peakCurvature,corner.curvature||0);run.reversal ||= corner.reversal;pendingStraight=0;
 }
 finish();
 // Join a continuous same-sign bend across a circuit's storage seam. Do not
 // join across unknown/straight boundaries; circuit closure must be explicit.
 if(closed&&runs.length>1){
  const first=runs[0],last=runs[runs.length-1];
  if(first.startIndex===0&&last.endIndex===n-1&&first.sign===last.sign){
   runs[0]={...last,endIndex:first.endIndex,wraps:true,angleDegrees:last.angleDegrees+first.angleDegrees,
    indices:[...last.indices,...first.indices],peakCurvature:Math.max(last.peakCurvature,first.peakCurvature),
    reversal:last.reversal||first.reversal,safetyPriority:last.angleDegrees+first.angleDegrees>=thresholdDegrees-1e-6};runs.pop();
  }
 }
 const unknown=corners.some(c=>c.status==='unknown')||gaps.length>0;
 return{status:unknown?'incomplete':'measured',thresholdDegrees,angleDefinition:'absolute change of forward heading, 0 straight and 180 reversal',
  wholeRaceChecked:input.coverage==='complete-event'&&input.resolutionVerified===true&&!unknown,
  sampledWholeEvent:input.coverage==='complete-event'&&!unknown,
  coverage:input.coverage||'unknown',horizontalOnly:true,resolutionVerified:input.resolutionVerified===true,maxSegmentLength,maxStraightGap,
  corners,runs,priorityCorners:runs.filter(r=>r.safetyPriority),gaps,
  limitations:['Sampled horizontal geometry, not a driving guarantee.','A gentle bend can be speed-limiting even below the priority angle.','Unobserved geometry is unknown, never straight.']};
}
// Advisory only. Caller must supply calibrated game-unit speed and deceleration.
// Distance to the final checked point bounds speed even if no corner was found.
function lookaheadAdvice({speed,cornerSpeed,distanceToCorner,availableDeceleration,reactionSeconds,marginDistance,knownHorizon}){
 const positive=[availableDeceleration];const nonnegative=[speed,cornerSpeed,distanceToCorner,reactionSeconds,marginDistance,knownHorizon];
 if(!positive.every(v=>Number.isFinite(v)&&v>0)||!nonnegative.every(v=>Number.isFinite(v)&&v>=0))return{status:'unknown',reason:'calibrated-physical-inputs-required',apply:false};
 const brakingDistance=Math.max(0,(speed*speed-cornerSpeed*cornerSpeed)/(2*availableDeceleration));
 const requiredDistance=brakingDistance+speed*reactionSeconds+marginDistance;
 // The target itself cannot be claimed observed past the checked horizon.
 const targetObserved=distanceToCorner<=knownHorizon;
 return{status:knownHorizon>=requiredDistance&&targetObserved?'observed-horizon-sufficient':'insufficient-horizon',
  targetObserved,
  brakingDistance,requiredDistance,shouldSlow:!targetObserved||distanceToCorner<=requiredDistance||knownHorizon<requiredDistance,
  apply:false,reason:'research-advice-only; preserve native controls until integrated and tested'};
}
const api={THRESHOLD,triple,inspectPolyline,lookaheadAdvice};root.__NFSU2_RACE_GEOMETRY__=api;if(typeof module==='object'&&module.exports)module.exports=api;
})(globalThis);

# Exact-build identity and native corner-record ordering

This is authored evidence and review metadata only. It contains no extracted native function bodies. No production or candidate runtime file was edited by this review.

## Artifact and method

All current-Wasm statements below were checked against `research/compatibility-93af6ccb/game.wasm` (38,205,596 bytes), SHA-256 `128e2b5816a8eace4b768aec920318a1613da8235801a361e2009e96550be1d6`, using the hash-checking `combined-v033-integration/tools/extract-next-functions.cjs`.

Guest instruction addresses refer to `research/opponent-handoff-current/SPEED2.EXE`, SHA-256 `f9dd86c054878ce6276beb07c1fd61874f7a1e4bf1f241b084c65b73e24168a7`. The older symbolic map was used to locate routines, not as a substitute for inspecting current bodies. Native tail jumps can be absorbed into their current-Wasm caller.

## Career event and heat identity

`G_CAREER` is the fixed guest object at `0x85ad40`. Current career event pointer is `[0x863470]`, namely Career+0x8730. A non-null event's hash is u32 at event+8. This is an event identity, not a unique attempt identity.

The current module's f18084 performs these operations in order:

1. Increments Career+0x872c, the starts counter (`0x86346c`).
2. Stores the event argument at Career+0x8730.
3. Reads the event hash at +8.
4. Calls f12766 with ECX=Career+0xd24 and the same event argument.

Native corroboration is 0x541167 onward and the call to 0x532ea0 at 0x541190. The starts counter is useful additional identity, but this review did NOT prove that every retry/restart increments it.

Heat state is not a guessed ordinal field:

- Results object: Career+0xd24 = `0x85ba64`.
- Heat array: results+0x54 = `0x85bab8`.
- Heat stride: `0xd24` bytes.
- Current heat pointer: `[results+0x34e4]` = `[0x85ef48]`.
- Heat count: u32 `[results+0x34e8]` = `[0x85ef4c]`.
- Within a heat: +0 i32 track, +4 i32 reverse (0/1), +8 i32 laps. +0x14 is a heat state, NOT the ordinal.

f12766 / native0x532ea0 resets current pointer and count, builds heat records, then initializes current pointer to results+0x54 if count>0 (native0x532fdf..0x532fee). Native capacity is four: count is compared with4 at0x532f22. The catalog's maximum three is an observed career-data limit, not the array capacity.

For event heat ordinal k, native setup uses:

- Signed16 track at event+0x18+4*k (0x532ee7).
- Reverse = byte[event+0x1a+4*k] & 1, converted to0/1 (0x532ee4..0x532f0d).
- Signed8 laps at event+0x1b+4*k (0x532f13).
- Signed8 event heat count at event+0x7e (0x532fcc, initial compare0x532ec3).

f1819 starts at guest0x54cae0 and absorbs its tail jump to0x541580. Exact current WAT adds0xd24 to currentHeatPtr and retains it only if less than results+0x54+count*0xd24; otherwise stores0. Native0x5415ad..0x5415d3 corroborates it. Thus a validated pointer difference gives a zero-based current heat ordinal even if two heats share track/reverse.

Recommended conservative reader:

1. Check committed pages and non-overlap for the fixed fields and every dynamic range before reads.
2. Require non-null committed event record (0x88 bytes), event count1..4, results count equal to event count and1..4.
3. Require current pointer >=0x85bab8, difference divisible by0xd24, ordinal<count; validate the accessed heat header.
4. Require heat track/reverse/laps to equal the selected event tuple. Require heat track/reverse to equal the actual running layout. Otherwise identity is unknown or reject the pending capture.
5. Capture event pointer/hash, starts counter, heat pointer/count/ordinal at the same native safe point as geometry, and compare to the requested identity. Page-thread reads alone do not make an atomic event snapshot.
6. For event pointer0, expose career event/heat as null/unknown. Never borrow retained career results for quick race. No general quick-race heat field was proven here.

## Loaded region

`[0x883dac]` is TrackInfo. Region is inline bytes at TrackInfo+0x40, NOT a pointer stored at +0x40. Exact f9177 loads0x883dac, adds64, and passes that address to native formatting/string consumers. Native examples:0x57a5a8..0x57a5bb and0x57a5f6..0x57a604. The next native string field is at+0x48. A checked bounded8-byte snapshot is suitable; do not follow an unbounded C string. An unreadable, missing or malformed region should be unknown.

Corroborating source: `research/upstream/runtime/game.h` G_TRACKINFO; `travel.c` travel_cmd where reporting uses `%.8s` at ti+0x40. TrackInfo track id at+0x8a has native consumers, e.g0x4125b4..0x4125ba. Region identity is useful for layout consistency, not an event or restart generation by itself.

## Restart limits

Race coordinator `[0x890118]` +0x14 is the race elapsed clock; source `runtime/career.c` compares it to seconds*4000. WorldTimer `[0x86518c]` is also4000Hz, so8000ticks is2seconds. A clock decrease or implausible unsigned delta must reject the pending sample and stop the recording.

These checks detect observed restarts. A polling reader does not prove an unobserved reset did not occur and advance again between observations. No universally unique native attempt counter was established. Do not promise perfect restart detection solely from pointers, the event hash, or the clock. Keep separate explicit recording runs and stop on observed lifecycle transitions.

## Five-point ordering and freshness

For a corner record at route+0xd4+i*0x80:

- XY pairs are offsets0,8,16,24,32.
- Corresponding route distances are f32 offsets0x28,0x2c,0x30,0x34,0x38.
- Signed center sample index is+0x74.
- Eight producer markers are bytes+0x75..+0x7c.

f17087 / native0x422780 resets all8 markers toFF before side producers (0x4227f0..0x422809). It calls f12713 with negative then positive sampling distance in mode1 (0x422831,0x422842). f12713 computes near/far signed distance targets around the native center distance, searches the route's node distances in the corresponding direction, and writes slots0/1 on the negative side and3/4 on the positive side:

- Negative output/markers:0x41fc8b..0x41fce2.
- Positive output/markers:0x41fbfc..0x41fc51.
- Early no-write return for an invalid starting node:0x41fd44..0x41fd4c.

f831 / native0x419000 consumes all five in that order, using consecutive distance differences (0x41908c..0x419230), constructs four interpolation intervals, and processes their ordered node spans. It modifies node lateral values, not the five slot ordering. The planner then supplies the middle three points in that same order to its curvature function at0x42289d.

Therefore `orderVerified:true` is supportable narrowly for a single native corner record when all8 markers are fresh/in-range, center index is within the verified native range, every point/distance is finite, and distances are strictly increasing. The current controller now requires that last condition. Do not interpret this boolean as verified ordering of a complete race, joins between separate records, closure, shortcuts, or uniform/resolution-verified spline samples. This review did not separately prove the center slot was newly generated on every planner pass; it is the native record's center, and freshness markers prove the four side samples were produced for the current pass.

The five-point cumulative-turn result is an analysis of those sampled chords only. It cannot establish missing bends, full bend boundaries or safe driving. Preserve `coverage: single-native-corner-record`, `resolutionVerified:false`, `wholeRaceChecked:false`, and explicit unknowns/gaps. Avoid concatenating windows based solely on storage order.

## Candidate review result

The ownership/module gate, committed mailbox/fixed-global pages, source/mailbox non-overlap,8000-tick expiry and observed clock-reset guards address the concrete issues reported in the first review. Opcode pre/post insertions preserve the existing argument stack and original locals/instructions. Authored observer stores are bounded to the2KiB mailbox. No new native calls or control/CPU writes were found in the observer.

Reran `node --test research/race-geometry-capture/candidate/tests/*.test.cjs` after the strict distance guard:23 tests pass. These are synthetic/offline preservation, controller, integration and compile tests. This is not live race validation, complete route acquisition, physical calibration, or a guarantee of braking performance.

+# Race geometry research candidate, based on v0.33
+
+This is an isolated test extension, version 0.33.1. It adds an optional recorder, not a new driving or braking feature. It has not been tested in a live race. Existing v0.33 controls and settings are unchanged. Disable other copies of Driving Tools before loading this candidate, and keep the working v0.33 folder for rollback.
+
+## What it records
+
+The recorder reads the owned driver's native race-planning window at the point where the game finishes its corner pass. It does not use free-roam GPS, the drawn map, screenshots, unrestricted asset downloads or opponent routes.
+
+- Off by default, session-only, separate from all driving settings.
+- Exact game build 93af6ccb only. Unknown builds do not activate it.
+- Offline single-player ordinary race AI only. Online/LAN, drag, drift, special-mode flags, free roam and unsupported ownership are excluded, regardless of the existing online toggle.
+- At most 256 windows, no faster than 10 requests/second, at most 40 nodes and 5 corner records per window. The recorder does not enable AI itself.
+- No new native calls, steering, throttle, brake, target-speed, tuning, race-state or opponent writes. New writes are confined to its local 2 KiB request/response mailbox.
+- Stops on observed identity/state changes, hidden/inactive tab, Stop, manual-control handback, game exit or timeout. An unsettled request or occupied mailbox requires a reload instead of automatic retries.
+- Export is a local JSON download. Nothing is uploaded or stored in a tool profile.
+
+## First bounded offline check
+
+1. Keep a backup of progress. Disable other Driving Tools copies, load this candidate's `extension` folder as an unpacked extension, and reload the game once. No reload or installation has been performed for you.
+2. Start an offline ordinary road race. Use the existing AI setting only if you want it to drive. Keep your existing working controls unchanged; capture does not require stronger pace, power, NOS or braking settings.
+3. Open Session & diagnostics → Race geometry research → Record native route samples. Keep the tab focused. Stop after a short run, then choose Export route samples. Export before reload/closing; re-arming starts a new recording.
+
+If the recorder reports zero sampled corner records, unknown data, a timeout or an unsupported state, report that result rather than assuming the road is straight. Export the partial recording if available. Do not repeatedly re-arm an unsettled request. Stop testing if the game behaves unexpectedly, and restore the working v0.33 extension.
+
+## Meaning of the 75-degree analysis
+
+The threshold is change of forward heading: 0° straight, 90° right-angle, 180° reversal. The analyzer combines same-direction turns within an ordered native record, so several gentler changes can reach 75°. Opposite-direction bends remain separate. Curvature below 75° is retained because a shallower bend may still need slowing at high speed.
+
+Fresh side-sample markers, finite XY/distances and strictly increasing native distances are required before a record is treated as ordered. Duplicate points, missing pages, stale native tails, non-finite values, invalid ordering and excessive spacing remain unknown. An apparently straight map or straight chord is never proof that the underlying road is straight.
+
+This analyzes sampled horizontal chords. It does not yet assemble windows into a complete race, verify the underlying spline between samples, detect all gentle bends spanning multiple windows, or measure altitude/banking. The native center is reused as the game's center; it is not claimed newly regenerated every pass.
+
+## Identity and coverage
+
+Career records include a verified event hash and native heat ordinal when the native pointer/count, event tuple, track, reverse and laps agree. Region is copied from a bounded TrackInfo field, and TrackInfo's track must agree. Quick-race career event/heat is explicitly unknown. Observed clock resets and career start-counter changes stop recording, but no universal attempt counter or perfect restart detection is claimed.
+
+Each window remains partial. Repeated records are not unique-corner counts. Export always says `wholeRaceChecked:false` and `uniqueCornersVerified:false`. Actual complete race routes captured or verified so far: zero. This is not an “all corners protected” release and does not establish safer braking, faster laps or fewer collisions.
+
+## Offline checks completed
+
+- 28 new synthetic/loader/UI/preservation tests.
+- 15 reader/geometry tests, including 144 synthetic unequal-segment triples checked against the exact native curvature helper.
+- 1,930 existing v0.33 regression tests. Release-packaging tests and signature-report writers were excluded from this copied regression harness; separate candidate packaging checks are recorded with the research artifacts.
+- The complete modified module validates and compiles. Compared with the verified v0.33 patch, only the intended route-updater function differs, and all its original instructions are retained.
+
+Synthetic tests and compilation do not replace live validation. The next useful input is a short offline JSON capture, followed by route-order, coverage and braking-horizon validation. No automatic slowing based on this recorder has been enabled.

+(function(root){
+'use strict';
+// Authored, read-only geometry analysis. This does not drive or modify the game.
+const THRESHOLD=75;
+const finitePoint=p=>Array.isArray(p)&&p.length===2&&p.every(Number.isFinite);
+function triple(a,b,c){
+ if(![a,b,c].every(finitePoint))return{status:'unknown',reason:'non-finite-point'};
+ const u=[b[0]-a[0],b[1]-a[1]],v=[c[0]-b[0],c[1]-b[1]],la=Math.hypot(...u),lb=Math.hypot(...v);
+ if(la<1e-5||lb<1e-5)return{status:'unknown',reason:'duplicate-or-near-duplicate'};
+ const cross=u[0]*v[1]-u[1]*v[0],dot=u[0]*v[0]+u[1]*v[1],theta=Math.atan2(cross,dot);
+ const angleDegrees=Math.abs(theta)*180/Math.PI,chord=Math.hypot(c[0]-a[0],c[1]-a[1]);
+ const reversal=angleDegrees>=179.5;
+ // A zero area at a collinear reversal is NOT a safe straight. The native
+ // curvature helper returns zero in this degeneracy; represent it explicitly.
+ const signedCurvature=chord>1e-5?2*cross/(la*lb*chord):null;
+ return{status:'measured',angleDegrees,signedAngleDegrees:theta*180/Math.PI,
+  signedCurvature,curvature:signedCurvature===null?null:Math.abs(signedCurvature),
+  segmentLengths:[la,lb],reversal,safetyPriority:angleDegrees>=THRESHOLD-1e-6};
+}
+function inspectPolyline(input,{thresholdDegrees=THRESHOLD,maxSegmentLength=100,maxStraightGap=25}={}){
+ if(!(thresholdDegrees>0&&thresholdDegrees<=180&&Number.isFinite(maxSegmentLength)&&maxSegmentLength>0&&Number.isFinite(maxStraightGap)&&maxStraightGap>=0))throw Error('invalid geometry policy');
+ if(!input||input.source!=='native-race-route'||input.orderVerified!==true||!Array.isArray(input.points)||input.points.length<3)
+  return{status:'unknown',reason:'ordered-race-geometry-required',wholeRaceChecked:false,priorityCorners:[],gaps:[]};
+ if(input.points.length>100000)throw Error('point budget exceeded');
+ const points=input.points,closed=input.closed===true,n=points.length,dist=[0],edges=[],gaps=[];
+ for(let i=0;i<n-(closed?0:1);i++){
+  const a=points[i],b=points[(i+1)%n];const length=finitePoint(a)&&finitePoint(b)?Math.hypot(b[0]-a[0],b[1]-a[1]):NaN;
+  const valid=Number.isFinite(length)&&length>=1e-5&&length<=maxSegmentLength;
+  edges.push({length,valid});if(!valid)gaps.push({edge:i,reason:!Number.isFinite(length)?'non-finite-point':length<1e-5?'duplicate-point':'sampling-gap'});
+  if(i<n-1)dist.push(Number.isFinite(length)?dist[i]+length:dist[i]);
+ }
+ const corners=[];
+ for(let i=closed?0:1;i<(closed?n:n-1);i++){
+  const before=(i+n-1)%n,after=i%n;
+  const t=triple(points[before],points[i],points[(i+1)%n]);
+  if(!edges[before]?.valid||!edges[after]?.valid||t.status!=='measured'){
+   corners.push({index:i,status:'unknown',reason:t.reason||'adjacent-sampling-gap'});continue;
+  }
+  corners.push({...t,index:i,distance:dist[i],safetyPriority:t.angleDegrees>=thresholdDegrees-1e-6});
+ }
+ // Accumulate same-direction curvature through real samples, rather than
+ // requiring any one polyline vertex to turn 75 degrees. Unknown edges and
+ // reversals of turn direction break the run. A long straight also breaks it.
+ const runs=[];let run=null,pendingStraight=0;
+ const finish=()=>{if(run){run.safetyPriority=run.angleDegrees>=thresholdDegrees-1e-6;runs.push(run);}run=null;pendingStraight=0;};
+ for(const corner of corners){
+  if(corner.status!=='measured'){finish();continue;}
+  const sign=Math.sign(corner.signedAngleDegrees);
+  if(corner.angleDegrees<1e-5){pendingStraight+=edges[corner.index]?.length||0;if(pendingStraight>maxStraightGap)finish();continue;}
+  if(run&&sign!==run.sign)finish();
+  if(!run)run={startIndex:corner.index,endIndex:corner.index,angleDegrees:0,sign,peakCurvature:0,indices:[],reversal:false};
+  run.endIndex=corner.index;run.indices.push(corner.index);run.angleDegrees+=corner.angleDegrees;
+  run.peakCurvature=Math.max(run.peakCurvature,corner.curvature||0);run.reversal ||= corner.reversal;pendingStraight=0;
+ }
+ finish();
+ // Join a continuous same-sign bend across a circuit's storage seam. Do not
+ // join across unknown/straight boundaries; circuit closure must be explicit.
+ if(closed&&runs.length>1){
+  const first=runs[0],last=runs[runs.length-1];
+  if(first.startIndex===0&&last.endIndex===n-1&&first.sign===last.sign){
+   runs[0]={...last,endIndex:first.endIndex,wraps:true,angleDegrees:last.angleDegrees+first.angleDegrees,
+    indices:[...last.indices,...first.indices],peakCurvature:Math.max(last.peakCurvature,first.peakCurvature),
+    reversal:last.reversal||first.reversal,safetyPriority:last.angleDegrees+first.angleDegrees>=thresholdDegrees-1e-6};runs.pop();
+  }
+ }
+ const unknown=corners.some(c=>c.status==='unknown')||gaps.length>0;
+ return{status:unknown?'incomplete':'measured',thresholdDegrees,angleDefinition:'absolute change of forward heading, 0 straight and 180 reversal',
+  wholeRaceChecked:input.coverage==='complete-event'&&input.resolutionVerified===true&&!unknown,
+  sampledWholeEvent:input.coverage==='complete-event'&&!unknown,
+  coverage:input.coverage||'unknown',horizontalOnly:true,resolutionVerified:input.resolutionVerified===true,maxSegmentLength,maxStraightGap,
+  corners,runs,priorityCorners:runs.filter(r=>r.safetyPriority),gaps,
+  limitations:['Sampled horizontal geometry, not a driving guarantee.','A gentle bend can be speed-limiting even below the priority angle.','Unobserved geometry is unknown, never straight.']};
+}
+// Advisory only. Caller must supply calibrated game-unit speed and deceleration.
+// Distance to the final checked point bounds speed even if no corner was found.
+function lookaheadAdvice({speed,cornerSpeed,distanceToCorner,availableDeceleration,reactionSeconds,marginDistance,knownHorizon}){

+ const requiredDistance=brakingDistance+speed*reactionSeconds+marginDistance;
+ // The target itself cannot be claimed observed past the checked horizon.
+ const targetObserved=distanceToCorner<=knownHorizon;
+ return{status:knownHorizon>=requiredDistance&&targetObserved?'observed-horizon-sufficient':'insufficient-horizon',
+  targetObserved,
+  brakingDistance,requiredDistance,shouldSlow:!targetObserved||distanceToCorner<=requiredDistance||knownHorizon<requiredDistance,
+  apply:false,reason:'research-advice-only; preserve native controls until integrated and tested'};

'use strict';
// Authored, read-only geometry analysis. This does not drive or modify the game.
const THRESHOLD=75;
const finitePoint=p=>Array.isArray(p)&&p.length===2&&p.every(Number.isFinite);
function triple(a,b,c){
 if(![a,b,c].every(finitePoint))return{status:'unknown',reason:'non-finite-point'};
 const u=[b[0]-a[0],b[1]-a[1]],v=[c[0]-b[0],c[1]-b[1]],la=Math.hypot(...u),lb=Math.hypot(...v);
 if(la<1e-5||lb<1e-5)return{status:'unknown',reason:'duplicate-or-near-duplicate'};
 const cross=u[0]*v[1]-u[1]*v[0],dot=u[0]*v[0]+u[1]*v[1],theta=Math.atan2(cross,dot);
 const angleDegrees=Math.abs(theta)*180/Math.PI,chord=Math.hypot(c[0]-a[0],c[1]-a[1]);
 const reversal=angleDegrees>=179.5;
 // A zero area at a collinear reversal is NOT a safe straight. The native
 // curvature helper returns zero in this degeneracy; represent it explicitly.
 const signedCurvature=chord>1e-5?2*cross/(la*lb*chord):null;
 return{status:'measured',angleDegrees,signedAngleDegrees:theta*180/Math.PI,
  signedCurvature,curvature:signedCurvature===null?null:Math.abs(signedCurvature),
  segmentLengths:[la,lb],reversal,safetyPriority:angleDegrees>=THRESHOLD-1e-6};
}
function inspectPolyline(input,{thresholdDegrees=THRESHOLD,maxSegmentLength=100,maxStraightGap=25}={}){
 if(!(thresholdDegrees>0&&thresholdDegrees<=180&&Number.isFinite(maxSegmentLength)&&maxSegmentLength>0&&Number.isFinite(maxStraightGap)&&maxStraightGap>=0))throw Error('invalid geometry policy');
 if(!input||input.source!=='native-race-route'||input.orderVerified!==true||!Array.isArray(input.points)||input.points.length<3)
  return{status:'unknown',reason:'ordered-race-geometry-required',wholeRaceChecked:false,priorityCorners:[],gaps:[]};
 if(input.points.length>100000)throw Error('point budget exceeded');
 const points=input.points,closed=input.closed===true,n=points.length,dist=[0],edges=[],gaps=[];
 for(let i=0;i<n-(closed?0:1);i++){
  const a=points[i],b=points[(i+1)%n];const length=finitePoint(a)&&finitePoint(b)?Math.hypot(b[0]-a[0],b[1]-a[1]):NaN;
  const valid=Number.isFinite(length)&&length>=1e-5&&length<=maxSegmentLength;
  edges.push({length,valid});if(!valid)gaps.push({edge:i,reason:!Number.isFinite(length)?'non-finite-point':length<1e-5?'duplicate-point':'sampling-gap'});
  if(i<n-1)dist.push(Number.isFinite(length)?dist[i]+length:dist[i]);
 }
 const corners=[];
 for(let i=closed?0:1;i<(closed?n:n-1);i++){
  const before=(i+n-1)%n,after=i%n;
  const t=triple(points[before],points[i],points[(i+1)%n]);
  if(!edges[before]?.valid||!edges[after]?.valid||t.status!=='measured'){
   corners.push({index:i,status:'unknown',reason:t.reason||'adjacent-sampling-gap'});continue;
  }
  corners.push({...t,index:i,distance:dist[i],safetyPriority:t.angleDegrees>=thresholdDegrees-1e-6});
 }
 // Accumulate same-direction curvature through real samples, rather than
 // requiring any one polyline vertex to turn 75 degrees. Unknown edges and
 // reversals of turn direction break the run. A long straight also breaks it.
 const runs=[];let run=null,pendingStraight=0;
 const finish=()=>{if(run){run.safetyPriority=run.angleDegrees>=thresholdDegrees-1e-6;runs.push(run);}run=null;pendingStraight=0;};
 for(const corner of corners){
  if(corner.status!=='measured'){finish();continue;}
  const sign=Math.sign(corner.signedAngleDegrees);
  if(corner.angleDegrees<1e-5){pendingStraight+=edges[corner.index]?.length||0;if(pendingStraight>maxStraightGap)finish();continue;}
  if(run&&sign!==run.sign)finish();
  if(!run)run={startIndex:corner.index,endIndex:corner.index,angleDegrees:0,sign,peakCurvature:0,indices:[],reversal:false};
  run.endIndex=corner.index;run.indices.push(corner.index);run.angleDegrees+=corner.angleDegrees;
  run.peakCurvature=Math.max(run.peakCurvature,corner.curvature||0);run.reversal ||= corner.reversal;pendingStraight=0;
 }
 finish();
 // Join a continuous same-sign bend across a circuit's storage seam. Do not
 // join across unknown/straight boundaries; circuit closure must be explicit.
 if(closed&&runs.length>1){
  const first=runs[0],last=runs[runs.length-1];
  if(first.startIndex===0&&last.endIndex===n-1&&first.sign===last.sign){
   runs[0]={...last,endIndex:first.endIndex,wraps:true,angleDegrees:last.angleDegrees+first.angleDegrees,
    indices:[...last.indices,...first.indices],peakCurvature:Math.max(last.peakCurvature,first.peakCurvature),
    reversal:last.reversal||first.reversal,safetyPriority:last.angleDegrees+first.angleDegrees>=thresholdDegrees-1e-6};runs.pop();
  }
 }
 const unknown=corners.some(c=>c.status==='unknown')||gaps.length>0;
 return{status:unknown?'incomplete':'measured',thresholdDegrees,angleDefinition:'absolute change of forward heading, 0 straight and 180 reversal',
  wholeRaceChecked:input.coverage==='complete-event'&&input.resolutionVerified===true&&!unknown,
  sampledWholeEvent:input.coverage==='complete-event'&&!unknown,
  coverage:input.coverage||'unknown',horizontalOnly:true,resolutionVerified:input.resolutionVerified===true,maxSegmentLength,maxStraightGap,
  corners,runs,priorityCorners:runs.filter(r=>r.safetyPriority),gaps,
  limitations:['Sampled horizontal geometry, not a driving guarantee.','A gentle bend can be speed-limiting even below the priority angle.','Unobserved geometry is unknown, never straight.']};
}
// Advisory only. Caller must supply calibrated game-unit speed and deceleration.
// Distance to the final checked point bounds speed even if no corner was found.
function lookaheadAdvice({speed,cornerSpeed,distanceToCorner,availableDeceleration,reactionSeconds,marginDistance,knownHorizon}){
 const positive=[availableDeceleration];const nonnegative=[speed,cornerSpeed,distanceToCorner,reactionSeconds,marginDistance,knownHorizon];
 if(!positive.every(v=>Number.isFinite(v)&&v>0)||!nonnegative.every(v=>Number.isFinite(v)&&v>=0))return{status:'unknown',reason:'calibrated-physical-inputs-required',apply:false};
 const brakingDistance=Math.max(0,(speed*speed-cornerSpeed*cornerSpeed)/(2*availableDeceleration));
 const requiredDistance=brakingDistance+speed*reactionSeconds+marginDistance;
 // The target itself cannot be claimed observed past the checked horizon.
 const targetObserved=distanceToCorner<=knownHorizon;
 return{status:knownHorizon>=requiredDistance&&targetObserved?'observed-horizon-sufficient':'insufficient-horizon',
  targetObserved,
  brakingDistance,requiredDistance,shouldSlow:!targetObserved||distanceToCorner<=requiredDistance||knownHorizon<requiredDistance,
  apply:false,reason:'research-advice-only; preserve native controls until integrated and tested'};
}
module.exports={THRESHOLD,triple,inspectPolyline,lookaheadAdvice};

# Independent review: v0.25 saved extension tool profiles

## Outcome

**No remaining code blocker found in the frozen source reviewed below.**

- 44/44 independently authored production-module and separate VM/DOM tests passed.
- 418/418 focused existing native Drag overheating, owned NOS and full-tuner page regressions passed.
- All 17 protected runtime/native scripts, every native builder, and every WASM fixture are byte-identical to frozen v0.24.
- Production worker/session/pointer checks, performance/grip restoration, native drift request guards, tuner command flow, and per-frame driving/Street X/online/Drag logic are unchanged. The per-frame comparison excludes one changed online OFF status label.
- Real Chromium UI/reload/layout tests **did not run**. Chromium exited before page launch because socket() was denied, including a reviewed escalation attempt. No alternate route was attempted. No live game, account, user save, online race or server was used.

This is source, deterministic controller/UI-model, and isolated native-fixture verification. It is not live driving validation or visual browser QA.

## Corrected findings

1. **Stop-token removal could revive an older automatic profile.** Startup now requires an existing verified token. First automatic enable persists a real token; removing it fails closed.
2. **Startup validation could become stale.** The second load refresh was removed, coherent storage reads are checked, and startup is read again immediately before DOM mount applies it. Independent tests cover Stop, auto disable, profile deletion and network-consent revocation while mount is delayed.
3. **Concurrent successful writes could lose a profile.** Optimistic localStorage comparison alone was non-atomic. The production page now serializes mutations through browser Web Locks. Tests prove two queued saves preserve both, stale queued updates fail, queued requests use captured intent, and own/cross-tab F9 invalidates startup requests before a delayed storage event. The synchronous module is intentionally storage-only; direct-core interleaving reproduction is retained as historical evidence, not an unmitigated UI path.
4. **Unreadable profile storage could permit stale legacy NOS/Drag/heat restoration.** Startup now suppresses those driving choices when the global Stop state cannot be checked. Tester and native drift selections retain their separate legacy semantics.
5. **Stop fallback and action ordering required care.** Same-tab session Stop survives transient persistent-storage failure. Failed/stale auto-enable no longer clears its latch first. Retrying F9 after storage recovery saves Stop and restores profile controls without reloading.

## Verified behavior

- Save as new, Update selected, Load selected and Delete selected use persistent named profiles. Automatic loading is a separate default-off action. Save/selection alone never loads a profile.
- Updating an automatic profile disables that automatic selection until explicitly enabled again. Deleting a profile leaves current controls unchanged and removes that profile's startup selection.
- Network restore consent is separately saved per profile. Without it, Load forces network permission, online traffic and online player/race no-clip off, regardless of current session permission.
- Load releases held assisted input and suspends existing controllers before assigning choices. It refuses a pending drift toggle or busy/pending dyno request; dyno cancellation is requested and the user must retry after completion. Existing tuner drafts, contexts, applied/staged objects and game save data are not replaced or serialized.
- F9 clears driving tools and network permission, preserves named profiles, pauses startup durably, and invalidates queued profile actions. It clears deferred profile-origin drift reapplication. A native drift toggle already sent remains pending until confirmation/timeout; F9 does not force native drift handling off. Tester and separately selected drift choices remain separate.
- Cross-tab Stop or revoked loaded-profile revision stops current driving choices. Storage events do not automatically activate edited profiles, and probe events do not loop.
- BFCache-style pagehide/pageshow handlers keep restored driving controls off and restart exactly one tick loop. This was tested by lifecycle events in the VM, not an actual browser BFCache navigation.
- Storage is bounded to 16 profiles, 48-character names and 32 KiB serialized storage accounting. Strict schemas reject wrong types, unknown fields, hostile keys, accessors, unsupported schema, duplicate identities and malformed/oversized data without overwriting it. Names are assigned as option text, not HTML.
- If browser Web Locks are missing or rejected, edits fail closed. Existing profiles can still be explicitly loaded when storage is valid. This capability path was tested with VM doubles, not a real browser.
- Drag heat behavior remains the existing local current-engine behavior: no repair of blown engines or lost races. The production native payloads and ownership/context guards are unchanged.

# Route-based native NOS gating, research only

No production code, game state, or installed extension was changed. This is a
design/evidence report for preserving native AI, high straight-line pace, and
native NOS availability/skill decisions while withholding boost before turns.

## Findings

1. A new check only in request gate `7395 / 0x40e390` cannot stop active NOS.
   Normal cancellation in `17404 / 0x42abd0` requires active NOS, false native
   eligibility, and a true minimum-duration predicate. The current ownership
   extension at byte offset 9784 covers this normal cancellation branch.
2. Native eligibility already reads private route speed caps. Its route helper
   `4114 / 0x412220` returns false if any later node cap is lower than the
   preceding node cap. This is useful evidence of upcoming deceleration, but
   it is not a complete straight-road classifier.
3. Native eligibility can still return true with a decreasing cap ahead: its
   speed/current-cap test is an alternative to the route-monotonicity timer.
   The ratio threshold is 0.8 for ordinary road and 1.0 for Outrun.
4. Even forcing eligibility false does not immediately cancel an active burst.
   `15836 / 0x408430` waits until elapsed time exceeds the skill table's minimum
   NOS duration. An authorized start therefore needs sufficient known runway
   for that duration, braking distance, and planner/update margin.
5. Keeping straight pace high is compatible with a narrow route boost veto.
   Do not reduce global pace, alter opponent behavior, force NOS, or infer a
   complete straight from a zero corner-record count.

## Exact native data flow

`0x40e390` starts by clearing companion+0x1ff. After its identity predicate, it
checks active NOS and calls driver virtual+0xa0 (`0x416f70 / 15998`) with the
state/context pointer. A true result sets companion+0x1ff. `0x420810 / 14434`
consumes that flag and retains native availability and activation routines.

Inside `0x416f70`:

- Argument is context=driver+0x54; car is `*[context]`.
- Main route is context+0x31c=driver+0x370.
- Signed byte context+0x308 selects a 0x30-byte sample at
  context+8+0x30*sampleIndex. Native route monotonicity starts from the DWORD
  at sample+0x28 (`0x4171ed` through `0x4171f8`).
- The lane/cap selector is DWORD context+0x30c=driver+0x360.
- For the current-cap comparison, signed byte route+0xad is used as a node
  index. -1 means no node. Otherwise the pointer comes from route+8+4*index,
  and `0x40afc0 / 8487` reads that node's selected cap.
- Selector 0 reads node+0x40. Selectors 2,3,4,5 read +0x44,+0x48,+0x4c,+0x50.
  Selector 1 and other values return zero. These are native selector semantics,
  not evidence that all lane-cap types mean curvature.
- Car+0x430 is the speed used in the native speed/cap ratio here.
- Driver+0x7b0 is the native timer used for a sustained nondecreasing route;
  the threshold at 0x783b68 is 1.0. Keep its native writes/behavior intact.

The route-monotonicity query checks all adjacent caps from the supplied start
index through the route tail. It does not examine node distances or geometry.
It returns true for a flat low-cap corner, an empty route, a one-node route,
and an index already at the tail. A drop before the supplied index is ignored.
An unrecognized selector produces zero/zero comparisons and also returns true.
These behaviors are directly tested, not suitable acceptance rules for new NOS.

## Cancellation and duration

Normal branch, `0x42b0e6` through `0x42b12a`:

1. Opponent identity, or the current authored owned-player acceptance.
2. `0x59fa30` confirms active NOS.
3. Virtual+0xa0=`0x416f70` must return false.
4. Virtual+0xb4=`0x408430` must return true.
5. Native `0x592500` stops NOS and virtual+0xa8=`0x41e500` records the stop
   time at driver+0x7ac.

The existing start ownership gates remain goal-restricted. The owned-player
cancellation acceptance must remain goal-independent so a recovery/Park/NULL
transition cannot suppress cleanup. Do not put a positive straight-only guard
on the cancellation acceptance itself: that would reject the stop at the very
moment it is needed.

There is an earlier, distinct branch at `0x42ad24` through `0x42ad5e`, using
`0x40d850` rather than `0x416f70`. The current authored offset 9784 does not
extend its identity predicate. No claim of full alternate-branch reachability
or cleanup coverage is made by this report.

For ordinary road/Outrun, `0x408430` computes
`(globalClock - driverStartTime) * float32(0.00025) > skillMinimum`.
The start time is driver+0x7a8; clock is 0x86518c. Minimum is
`*[0x81cb60] + 0x570 + 104*max(skill,0)` in the verified retail difficulty
payload. Actual skill 0–9 values are approximately:

`[0.5, 0.5, 1, 1, 1, 1.5, 1.5, 2, 2, 0.5]`.

These fields are not monotonic with skill. In particular skill9's minimum is
not skill8's 2.0. Native drag/forced-drag bypasses this duration check. Retain
that behavior and keep this road-corner design separate from drag.

## Narrow design recommendation

Use a shared, bounded, read-only `routeBoostSafe` calculation for the verified
owned player's current road route. A possible single native integration point
is an AND post-filter on `0x416f70`'s AL result, restricted to the known request
return address `0x40e3c5` and normal cancellation return `0x42b109`. Let the
original native body run first, preserving native timers, skill, availability,
and all ordinary-opponent results. This makes starts wait and lets the existing
normal cancellation path see loss of route eligibility. It is a design, not an
implemented or native-executed new hook.

The positive start proof needs all of the following, with exact thresholds
still requiring the parent's route/braking work and live validation:

- Existing owner/car/driver/backlink/lifecycle/mode/network checks.
- A verified private active main route, valid bounded node count and pointers,
  node+0x64 ownership, supported cap selector, and consistent current indexes.
- Finite positive cap/speed data and increasing forward node distance values.
  Unknown, incomplete, tail-only, stale, or malformed route data must not count
  as a proven long straight.
- A sufficiently long known forward interval without a limiting bend/cap.
  Use both planned geometry and resulting cap/braking envelope. Nondecreasing
  speed alone misses constant-radius corners; native cap 60 alone misses gentle
  curves that become limiting at a higher requested pace.
- Runway for native minimum burst duration plus stopping/braking requirements,
  using actual speed and a defensible upper bound on boosted acceleration.
  The latter bound and a live update-latency margin are not yet established.

The parent is separately proving compensation for post-route pace scaling.
Its planned effective corner/braking envelope is the appropriate input here;
do not treat a node's unscaled cap as the final high-pace target.

If immediate stopping of NOS is required when a new bend appears inside the
minimum-on interval, preserving that minimum absolutely cannot guarantee it.
Either prevent that start using sufficient validated runway or add an explicit,
owned-road-only route-hazard stop reason that ORs with (never suppresses) native
cancellation. Such an override requires a separate implementation/proof and
must still use native stop/reset behavior. Do not zero active timestamps or
resource/identity state as a shortcut.

## Reproduction and limits

Run from combined-v017:

`node research/straight-nos-v017/probe-native-nos-route.cjs`

The extraction utilities hash-check 78e2bb69 and 93af6ccb binaries. The probe
executes native 4114, 8487, 15836 and the exact x87 rounding dependencies for
both profiles. The only boundary is virtual skill dispatch, which returns the
specified skill 0–9. It uses the SHA256-verified existing retail DifficultyInfo
payload, with no fabricated timing table. It asserts x86 return/stack behavior
and no mutation of synthetic route, driver, skill data, or nodes.

Each profile passes 10 route cases, 8 cap-selector cases, 30 minimum-duration
cases, and 2 drag/forced-drag bypass cases: 100 cases total. Results are saved
in `native-nos-route-results.json`. Extracted native WAT in this research
directory is not extension release material.

This does not execute the whole native eligibility body, the whole cancellation
body, live physics, traffic, alternate planners, or a newly authored NOS guard.
There is no measured race, collision, lap-time, or complete gameplay validation.
Live route horizon/current-index consistency, route refresh behavior, supported
event coverage, boosted acceleration bounds, and safe high-pace lookahead remain
open. No production recommendation should claim those are already verified.

# Canonical road topology and lifetime mapping

Seven exact-native isolated tests pass. This is a source-mapping and fixture checkpoint, not live driving, an installed adapter or a complete allocator guarantee.

## Critical table correction

The canonical lookup at `0x88a334` contains **1500** primary slots, not2048. The11-bit owner field can represent2048 values, but that is not the physical array extent. The manager at `0x88a320` has:

- `+0x14`:1500 road-group pointers.
- `+0x1784`: active-group count, exactly where a fictitious slot1500 would be.
- `+0x1788`: active-group pointer list. These entries alias the canonical groups.
- `+0x2ef8/+0x2efc`: another count/list; `+0x434c/+0x4350`: another count/list.
- `+0x467c`: total group bytes; `+0x4680`: group count; `+0x4684`: total road nodes.

The upstream `runtime/walls.c` and `travel.c` scan2048 values, but deliberately skip values whose group `signed16(+0xa)` does not equal the loop index. That handles the adjacent count/list values. A validator that demands2048 unique live group pointers rejects valid game state and reads beyond the primary table.

Use1500 primary slots. Require a nonzero primary pointer's group `+0xa` to equal its primary slot, and each node's owner `u32(+0xc)&0x7ff` to match. Validate full finite bounds, indexed nodes, ranges and coherent current identity before use. A packed node/link owner>=1500 is unsupported, not permission to read the adjacent lists.

## Exact native lifecycle

The mapping script compares normalized historical/current bodies across the complete pinned module, checks uniqueness and records calls/hashes in `mapping.json`. Original module SHA256 is `128e2b5816a8eace4b768aec920318a1613da8235801a361e2009e96550be1d6`. Original game is compile-only. Only selected exact bodies execute in synthetic memory with no original data/start sections. The only exercised stub is guest delete, which records ordering and does not free actual memory.

- `0x5deb80`, current f17477: Paths chunk dispatcher. Type0x34121 calls group loader; type0x34122 publishes links at chunk+12, current and original counts `(chunkSize-4)/32` at0x883db4/+8.
- `0x5de1c0`, f16384: group loader. Starts at chunk+8, walks `0x8c + signed16(group+0x34)*56` bytes per group, publishes group at manager+0x14+4*u16(group+0xa), adjusts byte/group/node counters, then rebuilds active lists. Native code itself does not validate every malformed input; our fixtures use well-formed authored chunks.
- `0x5d9430`, f2622: rebuilds active lists from exactly1500 canonical slots, filtering group flagbit6. This changes list linkage in group+0/+4, and list arrays/counts, without making a new canonical table.
- `0x5e4820`, f11222: unload dispatcher. Type0x34121 calls group unload; type0x34122 zeros link pointer/current/original counts.
- `0x5e3ff0`, f10753: scans1500 primary slots, decrements counts and clears each group's canonical slot **before** guest delete. Groupflagbit0 means borrowed storage, so delete is skipped, but canonical ownership still clears. Rebuild follows.

There are additional topology mutation/rebuild operations. `0x5d98c0`/f3403 resets current link count from its original count. `0x5e2bd0`/f8878 can compact/update links and uses allocation/free. `0x5de990`/f17320 and `0x5d95f0`/f2934 rebuild parts of group topology. The surrounding native track setup around0x5e9f2c..0x5ea0ef calls these. Mapping the whole call chain and its current-function boundaries remains separate from the seven tests here; do not claim a load/unload hook alone covers every mutation.

## Supported integration reasoning

At the verified synchronous post-world boundary, current canonical membership and loader-derived extents provide real game-state provenance. Do not invent allocator receipt tokens merely because a reference test accepts such an object. A possible supported implementation re-resolves every used node from the current table each tick/query, checks complete bounded canonical topology and dependent geometry, and refuses any changed semantic topology/identity before invoking native helpers. Copied route choices must never make stale borrowed pointers authoritative.

This note does not by itself establish every source of mutation, absence of reentrant loader calls inside a native query, complete residency across world transitions, or safety of retaining unchecked pointers between frames. Either demonstrate those synchronous constraints and fresh validation, or add narrowly pinned invalidation at the actual relevant native lifecycle boundary. Pointer equality or hash equality alone must not be mislabeled proof of allocator lifetime.

The route reference at `../bounded-route-progress` was originally written with2048 physical slots. The reference and its ABI have now been corrected to1500 primary slots with canonical group-ID checks and three added regressions. Its ordered route and XYZ witness results are independent of the corrected canonical table extent, but its old table-admission contract is not a production-compatible supplier.

## Reproduce

`python research/topology-lifetime-mapping/map-native.py`

`node --test research/topology-lifetime-mapping/native.test.cjs`

Tests cover first/last primary slots, exact extent/counters, count and aliases beyond1500, active-list rebuild, borrowed and owned unload ordering, and link chunk load/unload. No game, browser, network, race join, installation, frozen candidate or third-party state was changed.

"""Map named historical functions to pinned exact93af code shape.
Writes only names, call indexes and hashes, never extracted game bodies.
All current functions are scanned; uniqueness is not limited to a guessed range.
"""

import json,re,hashlib

names=json.load(open(R/'guarded-hosted-join/reference-names.json'))
want={1374,2622,2934,3403,8878,10753,11222,16384,17320,17477}
def functions(p):
 i=None;b=[]
 for l in p.open():
  if l.startswith('  ('):
   if i is not None:yield i,b
   m=re.match(r'  \(func \(;([0-9]+);\)',l);i=int(m[1]) if m else None;b=[]
  if i is not None:b.append(l.rstrip())
 if i is not None:yield i,b

def norm(b):
 s='\n'.join(b[1:]);s=re.sub(r'\b(call|return_call|ref\.func) \d+',r'\1 CALLEE',s)
 return re.sub(r'(i32.const |offset=)(-?\d+)',lambda m:m[1]+('HOST' if (int(m[2])&0xffffffff)>=671088640 else m[2]),s)
def digest(b):return hashlib.sha256(norm(b).encode()).hexdigest()
a={i:b for i,b in functions(R/'compatibility-v011/old-numeric.wat') if i in want}
byHash={digest(b):i for i,b in a.items()};matches={i:[] for i in a};b={}
for j,lines in functions(R/'compatibility-93af6ccb/game.wat'):
 h=digest(lines)
 if h in byHash:matches[byHash[h]].append(j);b[j]=lines
result={}
for i in sorted(want):
 callee=[]
 if len(matches[i])==1:
  for x,y in zip(a[i],b[matches[i][0]]):
   ca=re.fullmatch(r'\s*call (\d+)',x);cb=re.fullmatch(r'\s*call (\d+)',y)
   if ca and cb:callee.append((names.get(ca[1],ca[1]),int(cb[1])))
 result[i]={'name':names.get(str(i)), 'matches':matches[i],'callees':list(dict.fromkeys(callee)),'normalizedSHA256':digest(a[i])}
(O/'mapping.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')
for i,r in result.items():print(i,r['name'],r['matches'],r['callees'])

# S42 stock-car snapshot investigation

## Finding and limits

The user screenshot shows version 0.31.0, solo Performance Tuning / Tune Settings, Circuit/Sprint slot 1, and `Tuner snapshot stopped [S42]: stock car data bounds`. The screenshot has no stock pointer, memory size or heap-window state. It does not identify which part of the bounds predicate failed. v0.33 retains this check unchanged, so a version update alone is not evidence of resolution.

A concrete compatibility bug is reproduced offline: the exact supported 93af6ccb game module supports a second guest heap span, while both the in-frame tuner capture and private native evaluator support only the original low span. Valid high-window stock data produces S42 in the shipped v0.33 bridge. The isolated candidate accepts that same data with stricter native-window checks and obtains identical native tuning results.

This is a proven supported-layout rejection and a tested fix for it, not proof that the screenshot's rejected pointer was in that window. Null, corrupt, released, runtime-gap or incomplete stock data must still be rejected. Live user retesting remains necessary.

## Exact sources

Supported module SHA-256: `128e2b5816a8eace4b768aec920318a1613da8235801a361e2009e96550be1d6`. Original module is local research only.

`research/upstream/runtime/guest_span.h` declares guest regions `[0,0x28000000)` and optionally `[0x50000000,0x7ffe0000)`. The intervening region belongs to runtime data, heap and stacks. The window stays below signed 2 GiB. `mem.c` activates it once with NFSU2_HEAP_WINDOW=1, initial memory reaching the upper boundary and runtime heap break no greater than 0x50000000. `heap.c` includes this range in its guest VA allocator and excludes the runtime gap.

These source statements were verified against native function 22067 (mem_window_init) and 22068 (mem_commit) from the exact supported binary. Their bodies match the pinned binary after canonicalizing equivalent padded LEB encodings. The proof executes the original control flow, with environment/heap-break/log services explicitly provided by the isolated fixture. No full original game module is instantiated.

Exact live globals in this build:
- Window low at 0x2974ff60, high at 0x2974ff64.
- Committed 16 KiB page bitmap at 0x29747f60, size 32 KiB.
- A high source is admissible only with the exact expected active window, actual memory reaching its top and every source page committed.

The stock pointer is read at 0x8a1ccc. Its table has 46 entries of 0x890 bytes, total 100,832 bytes. Native loader x86 0x636be0, exact WASM function 12483, handles chunk 0x34600 by setting the stock pointer to `(chunk + 0x17) & ~0xf` and iterating the 46 records. It does not restrict the pointer to the original low region. A null stock table can also arise when the corresponding chunk is unloaded (x86 0x61b460); the candidate does not treat null as valid.

Proof files: `native-window-proof.cjs`, `native-window-results.json`, `f22067-window.wat`, `f22068-span.wat`, `f12483-stock-loader.wat`, `source-hashes.json`. Original excerpts stay here and are never distributed.

Candidate: `../../tuner-s42-window-candidate`, based on frozen `../../combined-v033-integration`.

- Exact native proof: 5 activation cases and 12 commit-range cases, including insufficient memory, disabled environment, excessive runtime break and gap/out-of-window rejection.
- Candidate bridge: 8 new groups reproduce old S42, exercise each high source and combined sources, exact end/cross-page boundaries, all missing-page positions, changed window metadata, mailbox alias rejection and insufficient memory. Existing guards and Stage/Restore checks remain.

- Combined final suite: 1,955 passed, zero failures/skips/cancellations.

## Current artifacts

Reference 2f0ddd3b: 36,872,934 bytes;
SHA-256 `5e33ad2cb4c4cc6893dee7cbd4d6e9bfb0f59a349d218fddbb5e3331ca69bc34`.

New 78e2bb69: 38,170,601 bytes;
SHA-256 `df7b930bb293ffdf975f0735d93e0797d51bd137d0cbeabcaff87fc5a693c759`.

Defined-function counts changed from 23,851 to 23,893. Imported ABI declarations
are identical, with 37 imported functions.

Full old-to-new function candidates:

| Matching rule | Any match | Unique | Ambiguous |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Exact body + semantic signature | 16,638 | 15,608 | 1,030 |
| All instructions, direct-call IDs masked | 17,804 | 16,394 | 1,410 |
| Above plus high i32 constants masked | 18,091 | 16,642 | 1,449 |
| Above plus high memory offsets masked, optional | 23,736 | 21,925 | 1,811 |

These are candidate counts, not proven compatible functions. A body can retain
identical instructions yet call a different function after table/index changes.
Masked high constants can be ordinary values. The default heuristic preserves memory
offsets; the optional fourth mode masks high offsets and records them for review.
A miss can still be caused by table-slot relocation or an unrelated branch change
rather than a changed hook contract. Independent review found such cases here.

Useful candidate mappings already forwarded to the investigator:

- NOS wrapper 22742 → 22782: exact body and type.
- gcall 21739 → 21740: unique call-normalized body.
- pace wrapper 21262 → 21263: unique call-normalized body.
- Engine 17311, governor 9339, grip 11372/13094, corner 4653 and the nine selected
  dyno routines retain exact bodies at the same indices.
- Tiny helper 4576 has 138 exact candidates and 4577 has 137. First-match scans
  would be unsafe. The runtime manifest uses the uniquely identified helper 4578.

Detailed reports are the adjacent `*-exact.json`, `*-candidates.json`,
`critical-candidates.json` and `runtime-signatures-78e2bb69.json` files.

## Runtime behavior

`__NFSU2_SIGNATURES__.scan(bytes, __NFSU2_SIGNATURE_PROFILE__)` computes the full
module fingerprint, parses function/import types, filters candidate bodies by
length/type, and hashes them. It returns unique/ambiguous/missing anchors and
candidate-only/unresolved feature groups. `canEnable` and every feature's
`enabled` remain false. It never writes game memory or patches input bytes.

All 34 anchors match uniquely at their recorded indices in the reference build.
The new build yields 20 unique anchors and 14 missing anchors, no ambiguous
anchors when compared to the old manifest. Its separately reviewed latest
manifest gives 34 unique anchors at the expected indices. Both-reference tests
select the corresponding exact module, but still never enable features. Only
336 candidate bodies required hashing against the old manifest.
A local Node WebCrypto run before the additional full-module hash took about
150 ms; this is not a browser/gameplay performance measurement.

The runtime scanner is exact typed hashing, not a general opcode normalizer. More
permissive structural candidate generation currently runs offline. Future
automation should review transitive dependencies, indirect dispatch, ABI, memory
ownership, lifecycle and feature tests before activating a new profile. A game
update can legitimately require new authored bridge code; no signature scanner
can promise to eliminate that work.

A fourth offline-only `--mask-host-offsets` candidate mode and multi-reference runtime summaries were subsequently added. Both retain the no-activation rule. The completed offset-normalized report is `2f0ddd3b-to-78e2bb69-offset-candidates.json`; selected allocator and critical mappings are in `critical-offset-candidates.json`.

Ask for **a short extension diagnostic export from the bad URL run**, while Automatic driver is selected, and whether the failure is hitting walls, braking late, stopping/getting stuck, or being too slow. # S42 native guest-window candidate

Status: isolated implementation and authored verification complete. Independent review required before integration/release. Version intentionally remains 0.33.0. No user-facing artifact uploaded, no live game, installed extension or save changed.

## Problem

The user screenshot reports S42 stock-car data bounds in v0.31. This guard is unchanged in v0.33. Exact 93af6ccb supports an optional second guest heap span `[0x50000000,0x7ffe0000)`. The old tuner bridge and private evaluator reject all sources there. A valid high stock table reproduces S42 in the old bridge and succeeds in the candidate.

The screenshot does not contain the actual pointer/window state, so this is a demonstrated compatibility fix, not a confirmed account of that specific run. Invalid/null/released stock data must still fail. Full evidence: `research/tuner-s42-proof/FINDINGS.md`.

## Implementation scope

- Snapshot-only stock, rules, catalog and curve source checks may accept the exact high guest window. They require exact current native window globals, actual memory covering the window, complete committed-page coverage and no alias with the private mailbox. Low source behavior is unchanged. The runtime gap and addresses at/above the window's upper end remain forbidden.
- Each new page scan is bounded to eight pages or fewer by the existing stock/rule/catalog/curve count limits. There are no new native calls, no added locals and no widened live write destinations.
- Current ride/player/car/record/tune/parts/stack bounds, S20's exact static ride exception, source overlap checks, sequence/cancel/ownership guards, all 170 locals and the 16 MiB mailbox stay intact. Stage/Restore still write only active 41 bytes and the selected visit's 41 bytes. Saved records are not written.
- Private native memory may grow on demand to hold high captured ranges at their original addresses, with a maximum of 2 GiB. The initial allocation remains 704 MiB. Hydration validates all ranges before growth/copy, rejects the runtime gap and high ranges larger than the largest bounded capture, and refreshes the DataView after growth. Its view is exposed via a getter so callers never use a detached view.
- Existing private read/write barriers, captured-range permissions, CPU/stack isolation, fuel, rollback, target validation and native estimates remain. Memory growth is private and can fail cleanly if the browser cannot reserve it.
- Profile rebuilding permits only the exact shipped v0.29–v0.33 static-ride prefix (8,386 bytes, SHA-256 f01bf8bf917fb4a52fcabebfde08f925dd9136a14c17ae911dd79526791e51a0), in addition to prior exact migrations. Unknown/mutated/coercible prefixes still reject.
